Digitale Transformation (Herrmann, Kunze, Liebe, Treiber, Bernau) | DLD Campus 19
snippet.description:
Die Diskussion um die digitale Transformation bewegt inzwischen jedes Unternehmen. Wie stemme ich den digitalen Wandel im Unternehmen? Welches ist die richtige Herangehensweise? Wie können Mitarbeiter in diesem Veränderungsprozess „mitgenommen werden“? Wie nimmt man ihnen die Angst vor exponentiellen Technologien? Wie wird man den Erwartungen der Kunden gerecht? Inwieweit kann der Staat (und mit welchen Gesetzen) hier unterstützend wirken oder eingreifen?

Die Diskussionsrunde beleuchtet diese Fragen aus unterschiedlichen Perspektiven – aus Sicht eines mittelständischen Unternehmens, eines Start-ups, eines Global Players und einer internationalen Digitalplattform.

snippet.title: David vs. Goliath Internethandel der Zukunft (Boos, Bibra, Fridgen) | DLD Campus 19
Aktie, ledig, jung und extrem erfolgreich sucht Dich! (Alfred Maydorn, Börsenmedien) | DLD Campus 19
snippet.description: Die Aktie als Geldanlage ist alles andere als jung, schon im 15. Jahrhundert gab es die ersten Vorläufer der Börsen. Junge Aktionäre gibt es heute – leider – auch nur sehr wenige. Nur zehn Prozent der unter 40-jährigen sin Deutschland halten Aktien oder Aktienfonds. Dabei gibt es keine Geldanlage, die erfolgreicher ist und die darüber hinaus auch noch mehr Freude macht. Die Kombination aus Spaß und Freude bieten auch viele Jobs, die mit Aktien zu tun habe, etwa der des Wirtschaftsredakteurs.

Kunststoffe: Vom Problemlöser zum Problem (Christian Laforsch, Uni Bayreuth) | DLD Campus 19
snippet.description: Neben dem Klimawandel hat uns in den letzten Monaten kaum ein Thema so bewegt wie der Plastikmüll in den Weltmeeren und der Nachweis von Mikroplastik in heimischen Gewässern und unserer Nahrungskette. Christian Laforsch erforscht Bildung und Effekte von Mikroplastik. Er wird über den aktuellen Stand seiner Forschung berichten und Lösungsansätze für das Umweltproblem vorstellen.

snippet.title: Warum wir hierzulande mehr Optimismus brauchen (Wolfgang Kerler, 1E9) | DLD Campus 19
snippet.description: Wolfgang Kerler, Co-Founder der 1E9 Denkfabrik, ist davon überzeugt, dass die Zukunft nicht nur in China oder dem Silicon Valley gestaltet wird, sondern auch in Deutschland. Er wird erklären, wie Deutschland durch mehr Zusammenarbeit und eigene Zukunftsvisionen zum echten Technologie- und Ideen-Standort werden kann. Und er wird ein bisschen Optimismus verbreiten!

snippet.title: Ländliche Mobilität (Danzer, Soltes, Wippermann, Weiland, Schulze) | DLD Campus 19
snippet.description: Mit Blick auf Klimawandel und Nachhaltigkeit kommt dem Thema Mobilität eine wichtige Rolle zu, denn Fahr- und Flugzeuge tragen massiv zum Ausstoß von Schadstoffen bei. Während der Ausbau digitaler und nachhaltiger Mobilitätskonzepte vor allem in Großstädten stattfindet, stellt sich die Frage, wie der Wandel der Mobilität in ländlichen Regionen aussehen kann. Hier ist nach wie vor mindestens ein Auto pro Haushalt Pflicht, um das alltägliche Leben zu meistern. Gleichzeitig altert die Bevölkerung auf dem Land schneller, so dass technische, ökonomische und auch soziale Fragen im Bereich ländlicher Mobilität von großer Bedeutung sind. Die Diskussion fokussiert auf spezielle Anforderungen und mögliche Lösungen der Mobilität für ländliche Regionen.

snippet.title: Garantiert mobil – egal wo Du lebst (Katharina Schulze) | DLD Campus 19
snippet.description: Für die Grünen ist Mobilität eine wesentliche Grundlage für die Teilhabe am öffentlichen Leben. Unterwegs auf dem Land in Bayern bedeutet aber momentan mit dem eigenen Auto mobil zu sein, denn der wenig ausgebaute ÖPNV ist keine Alternative. Bei DLD Campus in Bayreuth spricht daher Katharina Schulze, Fraktionsvorsitzende der Grünen im Bayerischen Landtag, über grüne Ideen für Mobilität im ländlichen Raum. Digitale Systeme helfen dabei, die verschiedenen Verkehrsträger zu verbinden und auch über die Grenzen von Landkreisen, Verkehrsverbünden oder Preisstufen hinweg benutzbar zu machen.

snippet.title: Moonshot Innovation in exponentiellen Zeiten (Maks Giordano, Kreait)  | DLD Campus 19
snippet.description: Digitale Technologien entwickeln sich häufig nicht linear, sondern exponentiell. Das hat für Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft immense Auswirkungen. Maks Giordano wird beleuchten, wie wir exponentielle Technologien nutzen und unser Denken und Handeln im Sinne des „Moonshot Thinking“, also in Richtung ambitionierter und bahnbrechender Projekte, ausrichten können.

snippet.description:
Panlel with Alexander Görlach, Anke Domscheit-Berg, Carl Benedikt Frey, Peter Kropsch and Jeff Jarvis.
In this session, we want to explore the multifaceted impact of technology on the way we keep ourselves informed, the way we shape our opinions or, maybe, in which way they are being shaped in a world where there is a more and more segmented , sometimes even segregated „information sphere“. While the global connectivity of the internet promised us a world that could be more democratic, more free, more informed – with the knowledge of the world at our fingertips – the opposite seems to be the case: populism, fake news, hate speech are symptoms of a societal change that is driven by the transformative power of accelerated technology? Or what is behind it? How can we tackle it? What’s the role of political leaders, of journalists, of entrepreneurs and activists? How can we bridge the (information) gap between communities drifting further apart? These are some of the big questions of our time.

snippet.description: Artificial Intelligence may be the single most disruptive technology the world has seen since the Industrial Revolution. But is AI real? How are companies adopting and applying AI in their organizations today? What can you do to reimagine work for the age of AI? What will the role of people be? There’s a lot of talk and concern around people losing their jobs, but on the positive side - how can machines and humans work side-by-side? How will AI be paired with humans and how can business leaders help in this transition. Responsible AI – how can we balance the opportunity with the challenges when it comes to AI? What steps can governments and businesses take?

snippet.description: The panel discussion „Unicorns Made in Germany“ will explore the growth stories of Zalando, Delivery Hero and Auto1. The C-level executives of these three super successful tech companies from Germany will discuss in depth what made them successful and what they plan for the future. We will also talk about their international expansion and why it was good to start in Germany. Furthermore, we will debate the rising super-power of global tech giants like Amazon, Google, Facebook, Alibaba and Tencent and discuss what it means even for European unicorns. And whether or not and if yes then how the EU should intervene.

snippet.title: Highlights - Take Responsibility! (A. McAFee, A. Birken, D. Kirkpatrick) | DLD 18
Highlights - Mobility Hub Munich (Helmut Schönenberger, UnternehmerTUM) | DLD 18
Highlights - About Flying Taxis & High Speed Trains (Avezum, Hoke, Reuter, Williams) | DLD 18
Highlights - The Break Up Of Big Tech (Scott Galloway, L2) | DLD 18
Highlights - Human & Machine (Paul Daugherty, Accenture & Greg Williams, WIRED UK) | DLD 18
snippet.description: Artificial Intelligence may be the single most disruptive technology the world has seen since the Industrial Revolution. But is AI real? How are companies adopting and applying AI in their organizations today? What can you do to reimagine work for the age of AI? What will the role of people be? There’s a lot of talk and concern around people losing their jobs, but on the positive side - how can machines and humans work side-by-side? How will AI be paired with humans and how can business leaders help in this transition. Responsible AI – how can we balance the opportunity with the challenges when it comes to AI? What steps can governments and businesses take?

snippet.title: Highlights - Still Reconquering -- 365 Days Later (Swisher, Meckel, Rosen, Murphy) | DLD 18
Highlights - Reconquer Your Voice + DLD Impact Award Ceremony (McGowan, Kekilli) | DLD 18
Highlights - Only An Incubator -- Europe’s Competitive Edge (Mettler, Hinrikus, Ljungman) | DLD 18
snippet.description: Europe’s leadership in creating advancements for our society has faded away in the last years. The US and China are way ahead of us in using the grand opportunities that arise with the Internet and digital technologies and tend to use our continent as their incubator for innovation. The probability that Europe may grow the next wave of billion dollar companies and world-class innovation has never been higher. However, in times of transition, there is a true need for systemic change and re-engagement. What happens after Brexit? How can we empower more successful entrepreneurs and investors to pass on their knowledge and experience to those future entrepreneurs of tomorrow? Taveet Hinrikus (Transferwise), Mattias Ljungman (Atomico) moderated by Ann Mettler (European Political Strategy Centre) will discuss how Europe can reconquer its leading position in the next wave of the digital revolution.

snippet.title: Highlights - Tech Colonialism: Too Much World (Obrist, Steyerl, Morozov) | DLD 18
Highlights - How To Fix The Future (Andrew Keen & Paul-Bernhard Kallen) | DLD 18
Highlights - Building Community In A Polarized World (Elliot Schrage, Facebook) | DLD 18
Highlights - Rebels Remaking Video & Advertising (Andrew A. Rosen) | DLD 18
Highlights - Why Europe Should Embrace The World (S. Gabriel, A. Latour) | DLD 18
Business Ideas For The Future (Ijad Madisch & Seabstian Matthes) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: Ijad Madisch (ResearchGate) will talk with Sebastian Matthes (HuffPost Germany) about the future of science and research, in connection with new possibilities of automation. What will labs look like, and what kind of businesses might arise in this new world of science?

snippet.title: The Crypto Revolution – Why We Need Digital, Decentralised Cash (A. Koenig, bitfilm) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: The state monopoly on money leads to economic distortions and social injustice. A free competition of currencies, as it has been suggested by nobel laureate Friedrich August v. Hayek in the 1970s, would be a much better monetary system - but so far it was a utopia. Cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, Litecoin, Dash or Monero are the realisation of Hayek's vision.

snippet.title: Education for Integration I (G. Ruehl, Klöckner & Co & F. van Heerden, ReDI) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: In this session, Ferdi van Heerden will introduce the ReDI School of Digital Integration for tech interested newcomers applying for asylum in Germany. The non-profit digital school for tech-interested newcomers was founded in February 2016 by a team convinced that technology can bring people together to build new solutions to old problems. What is this project that Angela Merkel, Sheryl Sandberg and Mark Zuckerberg have showed interest in and visited in the last months?

snippet.title: Teaching Entrepreneurship (Bill Aulet, MIT & Thomas Andrae, Nucleus Scientific) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: Bill Aulet is changing the way entrepreneurship is understood, taught and practiced around the world. He is an award-winning educator and author whose current work is built off the foundation of his 25-year successful business career So, what does it take to be a good entrepreneur? Now a Professor of the Practice at MIT Sloan School of Management, Aulet will explain processes, most important tools and methods.

snippet.title: Education for Integration II (Eva Schatz & Viola Zimmer, Kuniri) | DLD Berlin 17
SevenVentures Pitch Day (Gaetjen, Winterscheidt, Thiel, Pauthner) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: For the second time, four promising start-ups will pitch head to head on the DLD stage at SevenVentures Pitch Day. Expect a tough competition for the million Euro media package prize. The winner will be chosen by the audience and an expert jury including presenter and investor Joko Winterscheidt and SevenVentures CEO Florian Pauthner. The show is moderated by Steven Gaetjen.

snippet.title: Welcome Back (Steffi Czerny, DLD) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: Welcome back to Day 2 of DLD Berlin!

snippet.title: To Be A User Or Not (aaajiao, artist) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: The work of Shanghai and Berlin-based artist and blogger aaajiao is deeply intertwined with the internet and digital technology. In his most recent projects, aaajiao has adopted a more extended scope of practices, borrowing elements from architecture, electronic music, performance arts, product design, even medicine, to portray the young generation harnessing the power of cyber technology and the ever-present social media. At DLD Berlin, aaajiao will present examples from his latest solo show „User, Love, High-Frequency Trading“ and present his project „Body Shadow“.

snippet.title: Open IoT Platforms (Christian Thaler-Wolski & Moritz Diekmann) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: In this session Christian Thaler Wolski (B2B SaaStartup & VC Fund Advisor) and Moritz Diekmann (Telefonica NEXT / geeny.io) will talk about how open IoT Platforms can drive additional consumer value and help you monetize “your” data. Do you want to learn more about why consumer IoT is still not taking off as predicted? What learnings from WhatsApp wiping out SMS revenue from telcos should be taken into consideration when planning the next consumer proposition? Or who should own the consumer's data in the end? Then join this session which looks at smart propositions from the user's perspective.

snippet.title: New Mobility In The Sharing Economy (Peter Beermann, Sixt & Greg Williams, WIRED) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: This session will be all about future mobility concepts and the sharing economy. Join us as we hear from Peter Beermann (Sixt) and Greg Williams (WIRED UK) how this will revolutionize urban mobility. What does this mean for (mobility) companies? What does it take to meet consumers’ needs? What’s the future of transportation and new marketplaces and how will autonomous cars change this landscape?

snippet.title: Eigenarten – A Pianist’s Thoughts On Digitization And Europe (I. Levit & G. Czöppan) | DLD Berlin 17
Education For The Future (Udo Bub, Thomas Bachem, Melissa Eddy) | DLD Berlin 17
Digital 3-Dimensional Notations As A Revolutionary Cultural Technique  (C. Lölkes) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: The previous culture techniques were based on a two-dimensional notation: words, sounds, numerals and images on the two-dimensional surface of paper. Words, images, sounds, digits can now be converted into data and data can be converted back into words, images, sounds, digits. But above all, a three-dimensional notation is possible today with the digital culture technique, for example drawing and painting in space with Google glasses. The lecture will show new, independently developed techniques.

snippet.title: Dear Next Bundesregierung: A Digital Agenda For The Coming Coalition | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: The German people have spoken, and three political parties — the CDU/CSU, Greens and Free Democrats — are currently negotiating the terms of their coalition government. Unlike previous campaigns, many of the candidates addressed digital issues as key elements of their platforms. And they are not alone: French President Emmanuel Macron has made bold proposals for European digital projects, such as innovation funds, and the EU recently held a digital summit in Estonia where heads of state committed to advancing digital issues. With so many ideas and plans circulating, we want to discuss what the key priorities should be for the next German federal government to help Europe and Germany develop a more dynamic digital economy. We’ll hear from a range of voices in politics, but also from those who are building European digital players.

snippet.title: Actively Tackling Digital Transformation (Jens Spahn, politician) | DLD Berlin 17
The Art Of Neural Networks (Josette Melchor, GAFFTA) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: As artists continue to use technology in new ways – innovative products, companies, and artworks are inspired. Josette Melchor´s presentation will highlight artistic projects expanding artificial intelligence and machine learning research.

snippet.title: Pushing The Boundaries Of AI (F. Westerheide, K. Speck, K. McCurdy, B. Parr) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: AI and new interfaces are advancing at an incredible speed and impact many aspects of our life and sectors such as society, education, finance or language. In this session, Fabian Westerheide (Asgard), Kate McCurdy (Babbel), Katja Speck (DigitalMarketExpert), Ben Parr (Octane AI) will define the term and the current technological status of AI. What are successful and realistic strategies when companies apply AI. What should companies be investing in and what’s a 20-year fantasy?

snippet.title: Creative Forces In Urban Landscapes (Piedayesh, Cardiner, Franzke. Rohleder) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: What is the future of Berlin? Leyla Piedayesh (Lala Berlin), Brock Cardiner and Stefan Franzke (Berlin Partner) will talk about what makes and drives this specific Berlin buzz. Fostering new businesses and creative talents is the aim of every town and city in the world. How does Berlin succeed? How is the role of fashion changing in an online-data-driven „social“ world? Being digital nomads, how do we express ourselves?

snippet.title: Commerce & Content Born Online (Hoermanseder, Fischer, Court, Fishman, Griese) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: Mobile & e-commerce are disrupting the fashion industry. Many new direct-to-consumer brands are evolving at the moment that offer consumers to buy high-quality designed products at lower prices. How to meet individual consumers’ needs? What kind of venture-backed brands are disrupting the retail value chain at the moment? What new approaches by e-commerce companies are employed to drive sales? How can they attract new customers and retain them at the same time? Join us as we hear from Ben Fishman (m.Gemi), Marina Hoermanseder (Designer), Delia Fischer (Westwing) and Frederic Court (Felix Capital) on how they build and grow their businesses and about the secret sauce of next generation e-commerce.

snippet.title: New Retail - Threat Or Thrill? (Leogrande, Ahlers, Heazlewood, Morrissey)  | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: With the rise of big data, retail is taking a huge leap towards more personalization and targeted offerings. Traditionally, customers have always been differentiated based on their preferences, age, gender, income bracket, interests, etc. In the data economy, granular data is much more available. Dynamic pricing in the travel market is already widely accepted and used by customers and retailers alike. Is personalization a service or a threat to the customer? Could personalization transform into discrimination? Torsten Ahlers (Otto Group Media), Jen Heazlewood (R/GA) and Jörn Leogrande (Wirecard) are going to discuss the question „Brave new customer- threat or thrill?“ with moderator Brian Morrissey (Digiday).

snippet.title: Leadership In The Digital Age (M. Broy, M. Haas, E. Denison, A. Aslan)  | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: Digital transformation does not just disrupt business, but also leadership. Elisabeth Denison (Deloitte), Markus Haas (Teléfonica Deutschland) and Manfred Broy (Zentrum Digitalisierung Bayern) will discuss with Dominik Wichmann (Looping Group) what is important for leadership in the digital age. What skills and know-how do managers need? How do you successfully drive digital change in a company? To what extent do classical management models have to adapt to digital transformation? What does the "democratization of knowledge" and transparency in the digital company mean for leadership? How do you guide your employees through the transformation, instead of losing them?

snippet.title: Creating Art From Energy (Eyal Gever, artist) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: Inspiring Keynote from our DLD friend Eyal Gever.

snippet.title: Business Creativity, Innovation And Friendship (Heilmann, Ruehl, Wurst, Czerny) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: When we talk about the business world of today, we speak of digital transformation, disruption, constant change, data driven business models, lean management, KPIs and so forth. All these concepts are necessary to grasp and have a good understanding of – since starting and running a business in the digital age is much different from doing so two decades back. Business processes, organizational structures and markets are radically different, success and failure are measured differently, but some fundamental core values of good business, however, remain unchanged: courage, creativity, trust, empathy and friendship. Let’s find out which role they play in the professional biographies of the panel of business executives moderated by Steffi Czerny.

snippet.title: Digital Car – Exciting Opportunities Ahead (Dieter May, BMW & William Boston, WSJ) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: BMW is a brand that is at the forefront of digital disruption, approaches have shifted from vehicle-centric to user-centric. Cars really have become an integrated part of customer`s digital lifestyle. Why is it so important to learn with and from customers to better understand their needs and how can we service the right things at the right time to our customers? Join us as we hear from Dieter May (BMW Group) and William Boston (The Wall Street Journal) on the opportunities of digital car.

snippet.title: Startups And Corporates – Beyond The Honeymoon? (Benedikt Schmaus, PwC Strategy&) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: Benedikt Schmaus will give a revue of client and startup collaboration experience with crucial marriage counseling included. He will talk about why courtship is easy and all exciting but living together happily less so. How corporates offer the wrong things to the right startups. What makes a - financial and operational - marriage long lasting?

snippet.title: Key Trends In The Future Of Work (Stewart Butterfield & Stefan Winners) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: What is the future of work? Co-Founder and CEO of Slack, Stewart Butterfield is going to discuss with Stefan Winners from Hubert Burda Media how the nature of work is changing. What role does technology play in helping young enterprises to evolve? What changes are AI and machine learning bringing; what are the advantages? Furthermore they will also touch upon opportunities for innovation, business and customer momentum in Germany.

snippet.title: Thoughts On The Tech Ecosystem (Klaus Hommels, Lakestar) | DLD Berlin17
snippet.description: Europe´s rise and potential downfall: The CEO of Lakestar, Klaus Hommels, will talk about Europe´s economic growth and its reasons over time. Germany has especially struggeled to "export" digital innovation in recent years. What does that mean for the future of Germany and Europe? What are the levers to strengthen Europe´s digital economy?

snippet.title: It’s Only The Beginning (Stefan Winners, Burda & Cherno Jobatey, HuffPo) | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: Digitization changes companies, products and value chains. An end to this transformation process is not in prospect. Stefan Winners, member of the Executive Board of Hubert Burda Media and responsible for digital businesses will discuss with journalist Cherno Jobatey, how you can prepare your company for these rapid changes.

snippet.title: Welcome (Steffi Czerny, DLD) | DLDBerlin 17
snippet.description: Steffi Czerny opens the first DLD Berlin!

snippet.title: The Highlights | DLD Berlin 17
snippet.description: Review the highlights of our first ever DLD Berlin!

snippet.title: The highlights | DLD Tel Aviv
snippet.description: A little highlight Cut for all the people who couldn´t attend DLD Tel Aviv 17

snippet.title: Welcome (Beate Merk, Free State of Bavaria & Steffi Czerny, DLD) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: Beate Merk and Steffi Czerny are openeing the second DLd Europe in Brussels

snippet.title: Thoughts On The Digital Ecosystem (Klaus Hommels, Lakestar) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: Europe´s rise and potential downfall: The CEO of Lakestar, Klaus Hommels, will talk about Europe´s economic growth and its reasons over time. Germany has especially struggeled to "export" digital innovation in recent years. What does that mean for the future of Germany and Europe? What are the levers to strengthen Europe´s digital economy?

snippet.title: State Of The European Internet Economy (Clark Parsons, IE.F) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: What is the state of the European Internet Economy? Clark Parsons, managing director of Internet Economy Foundation, will give an overview of Europe´s status. What are our strengths? Where are we helplessly weak? What are the new impulses from Emmanuel Macron and the German election campaign? What are changes that digitzation and Brexit will bring?

snippet.title: Potential Of Legal Tech (Stephan Breidenbach, knowledge tools) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: Legal Tech is the digital future of juridical work. It brings the chance of making the law acessible to everyone, but algorithms will also partially replace laywers. The potential of this change will be explained by Legal-Tech pioneer: Stephan Breidenbach, Partner at knowledge TooInternational Gmbh. His vision: "Access to law for everybody and more balance on the legal battlefield."

snippet.title: Opening Remarks (Paul-Bernhard Kallen, Hubert Burda Media ) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: Paul-Bernhard Kallen, Hubert Burda Media CEO and DLD Chairman, will kick off a day full of inspiring panels and set the ground for the following discussions with an opening note.

snippet.title: Building Successful Tech Ecosystems In Europe (Taavet Hinrikus & Ludwig Siegele) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: Building successful tech ecosystems in Europe: In a conversation with The Economist-journalist Ludwig Siegele, Taavet Hinrikus, co-founder of TransferWise, will discuss the potential and opportunities that come with tech and how to foster entrepreneurship and innovation in Europe. Will Europe ever produce a tech company like Google or Facebook or Amazon? No country's matched Silicon Valley yet but with tech clusters emerging from Singapore to Tel Aviv, what does Europe need to do to compete?

snippet.title: The Google Shopping Case Pt. 2 (Maurits Dolmans & Andrew Keen) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: What is Googles perspective on the Google shoping case: Lawyer Maurits Dolmans and Andrew Keen talk about the companies learnings for the future. How can we stop fighting yesterdays battles and cooperate earlier? When is the future sweet spot for legisative intervention? Innovation is in everyones best interests – how can we revive innovation and at the same time guarantee fair competition

snippet.title: Public Diplomacy (Silvio Gonzato, Carmen Romero, Ali Aslan) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: In times of political insecurity in our world, this session will highlight the importance of public diplomacy and discuss general challenges for foreign affairs. NATO’s Deputy Assistant Secretary General for Public Diplomacy, Carmen Romero, and Silvio Gonzato who serves as Director Strategic Communications, Parliamentary Affairs and General Affairs at EEAS will give us some insights on how each of their institutions face the new emerging communications challenges internally. What common challenges exist and what are areas where both can potentially cooperate in the future?

snippet.title: Building Dynamic Governmental Organisations (Schweitzer, Ferber, Kotka, Witter) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: This panel will circle all around how digital service deliveries, e-residency and big data transform the relationship between governments, business and citizens. How can we build up dynamic governmental organizations in the future and reboot governments.

snippet.title: Protecting Copyright! (H. Enßlin. A. Niebler, F. Drücke, S. Scherzer) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: This discussion will revolve around copyright from the viewpoint of publishers, tv stations and music companies: What is the current situation and what challenges are the intermediaries confronted with? How have platforms such as Google, Facebook, Snapchat etc. changed the industry? How is right clearance handled? What alignments and initiatives are working in the EU at the moment?

snippet.title: Driving At The Edge Of Tomorrow (Jakob Brombacher, Sixt & Dan Michaels) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: Digitization, increasing automation, and new business models have revolutionized industries, and automotive will be no exception. Technology-driven trends will change how industry players respond to changing consumer behaviour. Jakob Brombacher will talk with Dan Michaels about the paradigm shift and the new forms of mobility: Rent, share and interlink.

snippet.title: Transatlantic Data Flows (John Frank, Microsoft & Julia Fioretti, Reuters) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: The first EU-U.S. Privacy Shield review and the next round in Microsoft’s New York warrant case are two transatlantic data flow issues which will grab headlines in the coming months. Julia Fioretti, EU correspondent at Reuters, and John Frank, Microsoft Vice President for EU Government Affairs, will discuss what companies and governments should do to ensure peoples’ trust and confidence as transatlantic issues advance.

snippet.title: Brexit And The European Budget (Günther Oettinger,  & Ludwig Siegele) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: The European Commissioner for Budget and Human Resources Günther H. Oettinger will talk with The Economist journalist Ludwig Siegele about Brexit and the influence it will have on the digital single market.

snippet.title: Winter Is Coming! (Taavi Kotka, Entrepreneur) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: Estonia has the most advanced digital society in the world and now wants to grow its population from 1,3 million people to 10 million, using digital citizenship concept. Former Estonian government CIO and father of Estonia’s e-residency program, Taavi Kotka, will explain how the world becomes more and more borderless and how this will disrupt and redefine the way how governments provide public services.

snippet.title: Challenges Facing The EU - Answers From The Commission (M. Selmayr & J. W. Schäfer) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: Challenges Facing The EU - Answers From The Commission: Martin Selmayr, chief of staff to the president of the European Commission Jean-Claude Juncker, will explain in a conversation with Jan Wolf Schäfer what the most pressing topics for Europe are and how they can be tackled: Brexit, the German election campaign and its implication and State of the Union.

snippet.title: The Google Shopping Case Pt. 1 (Gary Reback, Carr & Ferrell & Andrew Keen, author) | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: In June 2017 the European Comission has fined Google € 2.42 billion for breaching EU antitrust rules.  Antitrust lawyer Gary Reback will explain the Google shopping case and the lessons the EU should have learned from it. Expect a lively discussion with internet critic Andrew Keen afterwards.

snippet.title: Highlights | DLD Europe 17
snippet.description: Highlights and Interviews from the 2nd DLD Europe in Brussels, Belgium

snippet.title: Hackers & Painters: Aditya Agarwal
Hackers & Painters: Florain Leibert
Hackers & Painters: Conrad Wolfram
Burda Bootcamp Interview with Philipp Wallner (MathWorks)
Burda Bootcamp Interview with Marcel Tilly (Microsoft)
Instagram Story (by Alexander Nast) | DLD Campus
Financing Growth & Venture (Kolev, Teichmann, v. Preysing, Wehselau, Räthke) | DLD Campus
snippet.description: Nachrichten über spektakuläre Börsengänge oder Exits erfolgreicher Unternehmen erreichen uns meist aus den USA. Aber auch hier in Deutschland stellt sich für jedes erfolgreiche Unternehmen die Frage: Wie finanziere ich weiteres Wachstum? Welcher Weg ist für welches Unternehmen der richtige und wer ist der richtige Partner? Experten aus Wirtschaft und Beratung geben Einblicke.

snippet.title: The Promise And Peril Of Technology (Hilary Mason & Andrew Keen) | DLD Campus
snippet.description: Technik und allgegenwärtige Vernetzung bestimmt unser Berufs- und Privatleben. Was sind die Chancen dieser Entwicklung? Und welche Risiken sollten wir nicht aus dem Blick verlieren. Eine New Yorker Digital-Unternehmerin und Datenwissenschaftlerin und ein Internetkritiker diskutieren. [Gespräch in englischer Sprache]

snippet.title: On Leadership (Herbert Henzler & Cherno Jobatey) | DLD Campus
The Future Of Mobility (S. Kayser, M. Wippermann, T. Andrae) | DLD Campus
snippet.description: Welche Technologien werden die Zukunft der Mobilität bestimmen? Unter dem Buzzword "autonomes Fahren" ist die Zukunft der Mobilität eines der spannendesten Themen unserer Zeit. Aber nicht nur künstliche Intelligenz ist entscheidend für das Fahrzeug der Zukunft, sondern auch die Antriebe, die Energieversorgung und die Bauweise sowie die verwendeten Materialien.

snippet.title: Welcome (Steffi Czerny, DLD Media & Stefan Leible, Universität Bayreuth) | DLD Campus
snippet.description: Universitätspräsident Stefan Leible und DLD-Gründerin Steffi Czerny geben einen Überblick über den Tag.

snippet.title: It´s Only The Beginning (Stefan Winners & Cherno Jobatey) | DLD Campus
snippet.description: Die Digitalisierung verändert Unternehmen, Produkte und Wertschöpfungsketten. Ein Ende dieses Transformationsprozesses ist nicht in Aussicht. Wie stellt man sein Unternehmen für diese rapiden Veränderungen auf?

snippet.title: Biofabrication (T. Scheibel, S. Handy, J. Schenker) | DLD Campus
snippet.description: Unter "Biofabrication" wird im allgemeinen Verständnis die Herstellung von Materialien aus biologischen "Rohstoffen", wie z.B. Fleisch oder Leder, das im Labor aus Zellen gezüchtet wird, verstanden. In dieser Session geht es um synthetisch hergestellte Spinnenseide aus Biopolymeren und weitere Materialien dieser Art, die ungeahnte Möglichkeiten für Textilien der Zukunft eröffnen. [Gespräch in englischer Sprache]

snippet.title: Der Slaf (Public Possession) | DLD Campus
snippet.description: Zwei DJs gestalten ein Buch über Schlaf (http://www.publicpossession.com/product/public-possession-10/). Was steckt dahinter? Marvin Schuhmann und Valentino Betz aka Public Possession sprechen über ihre ganz sicher nicht digitale Arbeit.

snippet.title: The Future Of Gaming (K. Boesky, J. Koubek) | DLD Campus
snippet.description: Nirgends sind virtuelle Welten so präsent wie in Computerspielen. Die Gaming-Branche treibt die technische Entwicklung im Bereich AR/VR voran. Was sind die neuesten Trends? Wo geht es hin? Und welche Anwendungen werden in Zukunft nicht nur im Bereich Gaming eine wichtie Rolle spielen? [Gespräch in Englisch]

snippet.description:
Curated by Uni Bayreuth

Let's talk business and new ideas! Fünf Geschäftsideen, fünf Start-ups aus dem Umfeld der Uni Bayreuth und ein jeweils fünfminütiger Pitch! Wer kann die Jury von seiner Geschäftsidee überzeugen? Es trat an:

snippet.title: Innovation & Entrepreneurship Oberfranken (Albert, Goblirsch, Kastner-Maresch, Männlein | DLD Campus
RoboAdvisory – The Future Of Investing (Dennis Riedl, Börsenmedien) | DLD Campus
snippet.description: Nicht erst seit den aktuellen Zeiten des Anlagenotstands suchen private wie institutionelle Investoren Alternativen zum Sparbuch. Der klassische Anlageberater der Hausbank vor Ort wird bei Privatanlegern dabei zunehmend durch die Nutzung digitaler Beratungsformen abgelöst. Gleichzeitig laufen algorithmisch betriebene Anlagesysteme, wie Robo Advisor, der durch Menschen gemanagten Kapitalverwaltung den Rang ab. Was macht Robo Advisor aus und wie schlagen Sie sich im Vergleich zu herkömmlichen Formen der Anlageberatung? Das Kulmbacher Unternehmen betreut Robo-Systeme seit mittlerweile 15 Jahren – einem wurde in diesem Jahr nun die Bestnote einer unabhängigen Ratinggesellschaft verliehen.

snippet.title: Leadership In Disruptive Times (G. Zedlmayer, Maren Kroll, Constanze Buchheim) | DLD Campus
snippet.description: Die digital vernetzte Welt in Zusammenhang mit immer leistungsfähigeren Computern treibt Technologien voran, die exponentiell wachsen: künstliche Intelligenz, Robotik, Genomik oder 3D-Druck sind hier die Schlagworte, die uns täglich begegnen. Doch was bedeuten die Auswirkungen dieser rasanten Veränderungen für uns? Wie gehen wir damit um, insbesondere im Berufsleben? Welche Kompetenzen sind wichtig, um in Zukunft erfolgreich zu sein?

snippet.title: Welcome to Biotopia (Auguste von Bayern, Biotopia) | DLD Campus
snippet.description: BIOTOPIA wird weltweit das erste Museum sein, das Verhalten sowie Natur- und Lebensprozesse in den Mittelpunkt stellt. Verhaltensweisen wie „Essen“, „Schlafen“ oder „Fortpflanzen“ sind Themen, die uns alle betreffen und uns mit anderen Organismen verbinden. Es ist ein Museum für alle: Eine Diskussions- und Kommunikationsplattform, die aktuellste Forschung erlebbar macht, ein interaktiver Lernort mit öffentlichen Laboren und vielseitigen Programmen, ein interdisziplinärer Raum, der Brücken schlägt zwischen Natur, Kultur, Kunst und Design. Dabei kann das künftige Museum auf den reichen Objektschatz der Staatlichen Naturwissenschaftlichen Sammlungen Bayerns zurückgreifen – etwa auf die mit elf Millionen Exemplaren größte Schmetterlingssammlung der Welt.

How Virtual Reality Will Create A Better Humankind (Dominic Eskofier, Nvidia) | DLD Campus
snippet.description: In this talk by Dominic Eskofier, Head of Virtual Reality for EMEAI at Nvidia, you'll learn about inspiring use cases for VR from the fields of health, training and education. VR is much more than just an entertainment device - it has the potential to change the world for the better.

snippet.title: Cyborgs - The Renaissance of our species (Neil Harbisson) | DLD Campus
snippet.description: Neil Harbisson, der erste staatlich anerkannte Cyborg, wird darüber sprechen, dass wir mithilfe von Technologie eine aktive Rolle in unserer eigenen biologischen Evolution spielen können. Wir können Technologie werden, anstatt sie nur zu benutzen oder zu tragen. Dies eröffnet die Möglichkeit, mehr Organe und Sinne zu haben als diejenigen, die biologisch angelegt sind. Durch die Verschmelzung mit der Technik können wir die Designer unseres eigenen Körpers und der Wahrnehmung werden. Sind wir Zeugen der Renaissance unserer Spezies? [Vortrag auf Englisch]

snippet.title: Driving Energy Innovations (Axel Kießling, TenneT) | DLD Campus
snippet.description: Die Energiewende ist in aller Munde, doch welche Faktoren sind neben dem Ausbau von erneuerbaren Energien noch wichtig für die erfolgreiche Umsetzung?

snippet.title: Disrupting Music & Business (Katharina Wagner, Steffi Czerny, Gisbert Rühl) | DLD Campus

Dennoch bringt die digitale Welt und Wirtschaft auch hier tiefgreifende Veränderungen mit sich. Wie verändert sich die Wertschöpfung, der Blick aufs Produkt? Und wie reagiert eine etablierte Organisation auf das disruptive Potential der Digitalisierung?

snippet.description: The claim “if you can make it there, you can make it anywhere” regarding the US market has lost its truth. How do the different markets and ecosystems in Asia, Europe and the U.S. work? Join this roundtable of outstanding investors to hear more on investment strategies, interesting industries and business models that are evolving for these markets.

Russia Today (Lisa Dickey, author) | DLD New York
snippet.description:
Russia is one of the most fascinating and dynamic countries on earth, but we know surprisingly little about the people who live there.

Over a course of 20 years, Lisa Dickey traveled across the whole of Russia, interviewing people from all walks of life in 11 different cities—from Vladivostok to St. Petersburg.

Hear from Lisa’s explorations on the dramatic changes in everything from technology to social norms, witnessing firsthand the evolution of Russia from its post-Soviet shellshock days to the present.

How did the people personally change over time and what do they think and believe in today?

snippet.title: Wait, What Makes A Great New Media Company? (June Cohen, Deron Triff, Steffi Czerny) | DLD New York
snippet.description: For 17 combined years, June and Deron led TED’s media enterprise, growing TED Talks from its initial concept to an audience of 1 billion views or listens each year. At DLD NYC they will talk about WaitWhat - a new, first-of-its-kind content incubator that invests in, develops and nurtures original media properties until they achieve great scale. WaitWhat’s first original property — Masters of Scale, a podcast featuring Reid Hoffman — just launched in early May.

snippet.title: Putting American Grocers Out of Business (Nathan Latka & Dominik Richter) | DLD New York
snippet.description: HelloFresh was launched in Europe in 2012 and quickly expanded into the most competitive market in the world, the United States. They've raised over $350 million and are now delivering 11 million meals and 22 million pounds of food every month. Grocery stores throw out approximately 25-30% of their food when it doesn't sell. Driven by demand first, HelloFresh doesn't have this problem which leads many to ask the question: With less waste, a direct to consumer model, and $350 million in funding, will HelloFresh put traditional grocers out of business?

snippet.title: Media - Now & Then (Sasha Savic, Eric Ashman, Brian Morrissey) | DLD New York
snippet.description: Products that agencies created 20 years ago differ a lot from today: the same counts for products that media companies create today. The landscape has changed and media has to embrace tech more and more to ensure its survival. What role does data play in the future of agencies and publishers? Will they sell creativity or data analysis

snippet.title: Machine Intelligence gets real (Todd Levy, Babak Hodjat, Drew Conway, Karin Klein) | DLD New York
snippet.description: Artificial intelligence / machine intelligence is moving from the lab into the real world. This will have major significance for business and society. How real are the changes already today and how can we apply this technology in our businesses?

snippet.title: Can Social Entrepreneurs Make America Great Again? (K. Frischen & M. Bishop) | DLD New York
snippet.description: The U.S. is a deeply divided country. More than two thirds of all nationally recognized social entrepreneurs live and work in four liberal coastal metropolises - NY, Boston, Washington DC, and the Bay Area - even though only 16% of the entire US population lives there. What is happening in the social innovation space in the South and in the Midwest of the U.S.? Two experts talked about the relevance of focusing on common sense space, rather than on what polarizes us?

snippet.title: Into The Dark? Digital Future vs. Enlightenment (Rudolf Schüßler & Steven Levy) | DLD New York
snippet.description: The enlightenment era (1700–1789) democratized thinking. Even ordinary people were told: ‘Dare to think for yourself!’. The Internet, with its promise of global equal access to all available knowledge, seems to cash this idea in. However, dependence on search engines and soon on the advice of (semi)-intelligent machines, threaten to bring back pre-enlightened times – times of intellectual dependence. Building on historical research on intellectual dependence and the regulation of opinion, the talk put the prospect of our digital future in perspective.

snippet.title: How To Fix The Future (A. Domscheit-Berg, ViaEurop-Deutschland & A. Keen, FutureCast) | DLD New York
snippet.description: How can the internet remain a force for good? We need a road map of what actions we can take―as individuals, businesses, and as a society―to ensure that the internet works for us, and not the other way around. Two outspoken experts will lead this panel ­- expect a sharp discussion!

snippet.title: Seven Ventures Pitchday (E-Y. Park, J. Gerbig, F. Pauthner, M. Butcher) | DLD New York
snippet.description:
For the second time, DLD hosted the Seven Ventures Pitch Day (7VPD).

Innovative consumer ideas across a range of industries were key for applicants from all over the US.

The following finalists have been choosen and will join the fight club moderated by Techcrunch UK's Mike Butcher:

- RISE Brewing Co., a NYC-local, organic, non-GMO, nitrogen-infused cold brew coffee company serving kegs and cans nationwide.
- Original Grain, unique timepieces that seamlessly integrate natural wood and steel with a focus on quality craftsmanship, authenticity, style and story.
- Supa, sportswear that conforms biometrics, sports, fashion and artificial intelligence.

SevenVentures is the investment arm of Germany’s largest digital and media powerhouse ProSiebenSat.1 Group.

Join the jury including the CEO of SevenVentures, Florian Pauthner, Chief Executive of Sales at SevenOne AdFactory, Eun-Kyung Park, and Founder/Managing Partner at Lieferando.de, Jörg Gerbig, for one of the hottest battles of the year and see those great companies competing for the opportunity to win a full-service media package to kick-start their expansion into Germany. Also the winner will be invited to the main 7VPD at DLDBerlin, 26-27 October.

snippet.description: How to keep a family company innovative? Jeff Maisel runs his German family company in fourth generation. The private brewery’s white beer is one of Bavaria’s most famous exports and the market is growing.

snippet.description: Yossi Vardi and Elliot Noss talking about Tucows. And why it isn´t named Threecows.

snippet.title: Time Well Spent: What’s Worth Our Attention? (Tristan Harris, Design Ethicist) | DLD New York
snippet.description: Tristan Harris (former google employee) about the war for atention and how not just The Big Four are battling to hold users on their plattforms.

snippet.title: Moving Beyond Apps – The Next Stage In Mobile And Messaging (Schläffer, Kirkpatrick) | DLD New York
snippet.description: What does it take for a company to compete with the digital heavyweights of our time? Data! And a vision how customers can discover and use services in a much simpler, contextual and personal way.

snippet.title: AI, The Missing Middle And The Future Of Work (Paul Dauhgerty, David Kirkpatrick) | DLD New York
snippet.description: Will AI create a whole new reality for the future of work? What lies at the intersection of humans and machines? How is AI changing the very nature of work and business processes. There is a Missing Middle on jobs and skills, and understanding the Missing Middle means opening doors to incredible value for businesses. A plethora of discussion and debate surrounds the subject of the job displacement AI will bring but will AI also create entirely new categories of human jobs emerging because of AI? The phenomenal promise and opportunity of AI also demands responsibility like never before. What can we do now to prepare for these challenges and to truly turn AI into society’s secret weapon for growth? Paul Daugherty, Chief Technology and Innovation Officer of Accenture, will dive into these topics with the latest, emerging thinking and insights.

snippet.title: Reaching Out To Generation Z (Melanie Mohr, Yeay & Brit Morin, Brit + Co) | DLD New York
snippet.description: Generation Z is the generation after Millennials. They are digital natives, who are setting the trends on how we communicate and consume media. Marketers are confronted with the challenge of how to reach this interest group. How do they tick? What persuades them?

snippet.title: Machine, Platform, Crowd (Andrew McAfee, MIT & Hilary Mason, Fast Forward Labs) | DLD New York
snippet.description: We live in strange times. A machine plays the strategy game “Go” better than any human; upstarts like Apple and Google destroy industry stalwarts such as Nokia; ideas from the crowd are repeatedly more innovative than corporate research labs. We must rethink the integration of minds and machines, of products and platforms, and of the core and the crowd. In all three cases, the balance now favors the second element of each pair, with massive implications for how we run our companies and live our lives.

snippet.title: Converge Or Die: Industrial Mashups In The Age Of Intelligence (Mendenhall, Brady) | DLD New York
Good People - Leadership In The Digital Age (Tony Tjan, The Cue Ball Group) | DLD New York
snippet.description: New technologies have made us more connected, transparent, and productive. But these new powers haven’t translated into better leadership—in fact, institutional trust has plummeted and employee engagement has stagnated. To solve these challenges, we need to refocus on what it means to be human, and what it means to be good. What qualities do good leaders have in common? What common crises make it so hard to be good? Anthony Tjan will suggest practical tools to practice goodness as a way of being, and make the case that hiring, mentoring, and working alongside good people is truly the only leadership decision that really matters.

snippet.title: 100 Days later - Is The Elephant Still In The Room? (Murphy, Haddad, Ryan, Swisher) | DLD New York
snippet.description: This will be a revival of the DLD17 panel in January in Munich. After 100 days with the Trump administration it is time to set the last months in context. It is a follow-up on the newest developments regarding Donald Trump’s presidency, his relationship with the media and how to cope with a new reality.

snippet.title: Fake News and Strat. Disinformation (Jarvis,Chopra,Blumenstein,Borthwick,Mannteufel) | DLD New York
snippet.description:
From Fake News To Strategic Disinformation

This panel will focus on the positive outcome of the attention given to fake news: the opportunity to fuel a flight to quality, proving advertisers and platforms with the data and cover to fund, promote, and support credible news and media. The discussion will be broadened past blaming platforms to include other affected and responsible parties, including ad networks, brands, ad agencies, PR companies, technologists, and political and government entities. How are these affected by online propaganda and fraud and what can each of the panelists help to improve the situation and support credible journalism?

snippet.title: Digital Transformation-From The Why To The How (Tarkoff,Schlaubitz,Garfield,Wolcott) | DLD New York
snippet.description: Digital has reached a tipping point. It is now the preferred channel for consumers to have their questions answered, and those forward-looking brands that crack the code and provide fantastic experiences on digital will endure. Brands know this, and accept that digital is the new reality, but implementing it the right way is easier said than done.

snippet.description:
Cloud computing and digital platforms offer huge benefits for people around the world. But the rise of large and powerful global technology platforms owned by commercial companies raises fundamental questions. What kind of rights, rules and responsibilities should govern this new landscape? What is the role of nation-states, when technology is global and data moves seamlessly across international borders? What kind of rules will best insure that tech is a force for good? Who should set them? And how can tech companies, governments and civil society best begin to address these issues?

Brad Smith, Microsoft in conversation with David Kirkpatrick, Techonomy Media.

snippet.title: Keynote Speech (Isaac Lee) | DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: Isaac Lee (Chief News, Entertainment & Digital Officer of Univision Communications Inc.) explains how Univision Communication turned from a medium size media group with a focus on Hispanic people to the biggest digital media company in America within 18 months. He shows how the company decided which other companies they had to take over and shows the motives behind each acquisition. Lee also gives a forecast on the future plans of Univision Communications.

snippet.title: Fireside Chat (Barak Berkowitz, Dave McClure) | DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: Dave McClure (Founding Partner of 500startups) presents the investment strategy of 500startups, which is a startup financing fund. The strategy behind 500startups differentiates a lot from normal funds because they invest in up to 200 startups a year to achieve predictable revenue.

snippet.title: Makers’ Movement (Bash, van den Ende, Gerstein, Melamed, Rotem, Schweitzer) | DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: In the Maker´s Movement talk makers from the robotic and creative sector explain and discuss how their ideas will be implemented, why their ideas will change the future and how a maker has to think in general. Matan Melame (Founder & CEO of Iron Drone) for example talks about effective drone defense, Arie van den Ende (Co-Founder & Advisor of RoboValley) presents the Dutch RoboValley and Yuval Gerstein (Creator of GRIDI) explains the new music machine he invented.

snippet.title: Fireside Chat (Maxine Fassberg, Hiren Majmudar) | DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: Maxine Fassberg (Vice President, International Site Operations Group & General Manage, Intel Israel) and Hiren Majmudar (Sr. Director, Corporate Semiconductor IP Business Development, Intel Corporation) display what kind of products and companies Intel is interested in worldwide as well as also in Israel, how they want to invest and how they try to join and support the Israeli ecosystem. They also show how successful Intel is in Israel but also how successful Israeli companies are in the technology sector.

snippet.title: Mobility (Renz, Adinolfi, Bustarret, Evron, von Hagen, Oelke, Tziperman) | DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: A High class panel shares their thoughts on what mobility means for them today and in the future. They discuss the necessary change and the future of mobility and the problems which will come up such as even worse traffic jams or the supply of the growing population. They also talk about possible future scenarios such as a mobile phone which connects to as many different parts in our life as possible and collects data to organize our time more productive.

snippet.title: Fireside Chat (Orr Hirschauge, David Eun) | DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: David Eun (President of Samsung NEXT, The Global Innovation Center) explains the structure and working strategy of Samsung NEXT which is a department of Samsung, focusing on supporting Startups and planning their future business strategy to really make them successful. He also names the other Samsung companies working in Israel and explains in which kind of startups Samsung is interested in.

snippet.title: The Multinational’s Role in Israel (Suliman, Dodge, Ramon, Teeni, Weisfeld) | DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: Represents from Microsoft, Google, Intel and Facebook are discussing the roles multinationals in Israel and how Israel has become a hub for technology, engineering and startups.

snippet.title: The Future of Israel & Europe`s Relationship (Oren Nahari, Dr. Beate Merk) | DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: Oren Nahari the Foreign News Editor at Ch. 1 and Dr. Beate Merk, Bavarian State Minister for European Affairs and International Relations debate about how globalization itself changes and how to tackle the risks of it. They also talk about the relationship between Israel and Europe, Germany and especially Bavaria and why both countries should work together even stronger and why Israel and other countries should invest money in Bavaria.

snippet.title: Financing the High-Tech Industry (Cukierman, Diamond, Geva, Oron, Rajwani) | DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: Edouard Cukierman (Chairman of Cukierman & Co. Investment House) discusses together with Colin Diamond (Capital Markets Partner, White & Case) and Yair Geva (Co-Head of HiTech Department, Herzog Fox & Neeman) and Yifat Oron (CEO of LeumiTech) and Suraj Rajwani (Managing Partner at Double Rock) the positive development of the Israeli High-Tech Industry and the possibilities of further funding this sector.

snippet.title: The Food Tech Revolution (Danielle Gould)| DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: Big data, robotics and tracking are relative new phenomena in the context of food. The world of food is changing dramatically, the past years the majority of the markets shares have altered from the largest food companies to small and midsized. The CEO of Food+Tech Connect are explaining how to keep up with the food tech revolution, the latest news and an overview of the key innovations within the food area.

snippet.title: Keynote Speech (Avi Hasson) | DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: Avi Hasson (Chief Scientist, Ministry of Economy & Industry, Chairman, Israel Innovation Authority) explains the development of companies in Israel during the last 15 years as well as today and also the challenges the Israel Innovation Authorities have to tackle in the next two decades.

snippet.title: Breakthrough Technologies (Barzilay, Bachelet, Bash, Dykan, Wolf)| DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: This panel is debating regarding one of the biggest challenges of the century- breakthrough technologies. The possible input of for example autonomous cars, drones and robots instead of humans will alter the way we are used to live. Breakthrough technologies are certainly facilitating, however the new techniques raises question. How safe is the new technology? How morally and ethical correct are the innovation? What impact will it have on humans?

snippet.title: Building a Unicorn in Israel (Globerman, Maniv, Moran, Waiser) | DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: Dov Moran (Managing Partner, Grove Ventures) and Eldad Maniv (President and COO of Taboola) and Shahar Waiser (Founder of Gett) are discussing the definition of deep technology, unicorn companies in Israel and whether Taboola and Gett are unicorn companies. They also outline the Israeli role in terms such as encouraging startups or being an attractive country for big companies to settle down in. Also they explain which properties a startup needs to be successful.

snippet.title: Media (Vardi, Deen, Olmert, Purie, Rechtman) | DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: In a world where media are playing a more important part and multimedia companies are constantly expanding, this panel is discussion the future of media. At the market today, varying actors like traditional publish house, startups and multimedia companies are operating together. New platforms are arising enabling people to engage, share and take part of media in new ways.

snippet.title: Fireside Chat (Yossi Vardi, Axelle Lemaire, Stéphane Richard) | DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: Axelle Lemaire, Minister of State for the Digital Sector, Government of France talks about the French interests in Israel as an innovation-friendly country and in startups in general; alternating with Stéphane Richard, Chief Executive & Chairman of the French telecommunications corporation Orange, who describes their system of open innovation and their strategy of collaborating with startups.

snippet.title: Autonomous Machines (Sven Scheuble, Ariel Avitan, Ari Yakir, Ari Zoldan) | DLD Tel Aviv 16
snippet.description: Autonomous machines, machines that proceed without the need of human interfering, might within a close future be available on the market. The development of the technology has the last years speeded surprisingly fast; the use of autonomous machines might already be accessible to the public in a few years. However, the legalization and other important questions are not developing in the same pace as the technology. Who will be the main actors on the market? Who are legally responsible for the machines? Can you completely trust the machines from a safety aspect?

snippet.title: The New Normal - Global Migration (Solveigh Hieronimus, McKinsey&Co) | DLDeurope 16
snippet.description:
Europe is a very special case in global migration but it is probably here to stay, it is the new normal. Since the post world war 2 era there has never been such a volume of people migrating from to developing to developed countries cause typically people flee either internally in their own country or to neighbouring countries.

Solveigh Hieronimus, Partner at McKinsey & Co elaborates in this panel her conclusions on why Europe is a special case in global migration and what the opportunities are.

snippet.title: Transformational Deep Tech (Candance Johnson, Martin Bruncko, Jennifer Lachman) | DLDeurope 16
snippet.description:
Startups must face some challenges when it comes to areas such as funding or regulation. This challenges are specially present when we talk about deep tech initiatives like flying to the moon or building flying cars, really out of the box ideas that require extremely risky investments. 
Candance Johnson (serial entrepreneur and President of the EBAN) and Martin Bruncko (chief strategy officer at AeroMobil) debate the question of how to foster a new ecosystem for the Deep Tech industries. 
Moderated by Jennifer Lachman (XING).

snippet.title: How to Handle European Public Policy (Lutz Guellner, Markus Ferber, Florian Eder) | DLDeurope 16
snippet.description:
The outcome of a meeting of a high level European institution with the heads of state and government is broken down in 28 different outcomes, what does this mean for handling and communicating European Public Policy?

Markus Ferber (Member of the European Parliament) and Lutz Guellner (Head of Unit, Information, Communication and Civil Society of the European Commission) discuss the topic, moderated by Florian Eder (Managing Editor at POLITICO).

snippet.title: Hacking Bureaucracy (Laura Citron, John Farmer, Adam Bonnifield, Ann Metler) | DLDeurope 16
snippet.description:
It is widely recognized that bureaucracy is a major impediment to competitiveness and innovation but it is also known that it's notoriously difficult to get rid of it not only in the public sector but also in private companies. 
This panel is about how you can hack bureaucracy, how to fight fear of risk and institutional legacy encouraging change in organizations. 
New digital technologies and the new generation of digital natives can be two powerful tools for transformation and civic improvement.

snippet.title: Empowering Europe's Competitiveness (S.Scheuble, A.Schwab, S.Rejal, R.Wauters) | DLDeurope 16
snippet.description: When it comes to entrepreneurship, all eyes are usually focused on the Silicon Valley, but away from this hub, Europe also offers a brilliant home to succesful startups. In this session we will explore how to scale companies globally – from US to EU and vice versa. What are benefits and examples for startups corporating with large companies. How can we facilitate access to finance and foster entrepreneurship within the EU to create a supportive environment for young companies and by that empower Europe’s competitiveness.

snippet.title: The Power of Words: Views on Turkey and Europe (Elif Shafak & Ali Aslan) | DLDeurope 16
snippet.description: Elif Shafak is a Turkish award-winning author and one of the most prominent and internationally recognized female writers in Turkey. In this panel conducted by TV-host & journalist Ali Aslan she will share her views about the missconceptions and prejudices between Turkey and Europe from both sides and the role played by Social Media.

snippet.title: Innovation: Europe at the Crossroads (Richard Allan, Facebook & Ryan Heath, Politico) | DLDeurope 16
snippet.description: Richard Allan will join Politico’s Ryan Heath in conversation about the importance of innovation for Europe’s digital future. The tech industry and creators in Europe are pushing the boundaries of innovation. But are Europe’s policy makers making the right choices when it comes to encouraging and nurturing that innovation? And what exactly is Facebook contributing to that effort in Europe? Richard will talk about the hard choices that the EU will need to make if it is going to succeed in a fiercely competitive and global environment.

snippet.title: Israel & Europe: A Synergetic Collaboration (Yossi Vardi & Steffi Czerny) | DLDeurope 16
snippet.description: Yossi Vardi, chairman of DLD Media, hs been one of the most prominent figures in Israel's high-tech industry over the last 15 years. He talks in this panel about the so-called startup nation, how a country with 8M people achieved to build 7K startups? What makes Israel so good in early stage startups?

snippet.title: New Challenges in Cyber Security (Mascolo, Vershbow, Ischinger) | DLDeurope 16
snippet.description:
BETWEEN WEST COAST AND WEST POINT - NEW CHALLENGES IN (CYBER) SECURITY

Chaired by the Munich Security Conference.

Freedom and security in cyberspace matter tremendously for businesses, strategists and society as a whole. Only through close collaboration, we will be able to set the conditions for an Internet that is free, secure and open. How can we effectively counter the growing threats from cyberspace while also strengthening the factors that underpin a free and open web?
Ambassador Wolfgang Ischinger, chairman of the Munich Security Conference moderates this panel debating the cyber security topic with Georg Mascolo (harvard University) and Alexander Vershbow (NATO).

snippet.title: Data and Privacy: Leveling the Playing Field in Europe (J.Waterworth, CCIA & A.Keen) | DLDeurope 16
snippet.description: American tech companies are dominant in Europe, between Google and Facebook control most of the revenue. How can a startup consider compiting with this kind of dominance? What are the challenges for European firms to grow? How does regulation affect this business enviroment? What are the differences between the American, the European and the Asian ecosystems?

snippet.title: Europe's Digital Future (M.Schaake, D.Dixon-Thayer, L.Griffin, C.Parsons) | DLDeurope 16
snippet.description:
Everyone in Brussels and across Europe is working towards the notion of a Digital Single Market in order to adapt to how fast the world is changing and take away unnecesary barriers that prevent startups from scaling among Europeans, but what are the promises of this Digital Single Market?
In this panel the Digital Future of Europe is discussed from different perspectives represented by Linda Griffin (global policy manager of King), Marietje Schaake (member of the European Parliament and one of the main experts in Brussels on Digital) and Denelle Dixon-Thayer (chief legal and business officer of Mozilla).
Moderated by Clark Parsons, Managing Director at the Internet Economy Foundation.

snippet.title: The Music Ecosystem: Embracing Dynamic Change (F.Briegmann, UMG & D.Wichmann) | DLDeurope 16
snippet.description:
THE MUSIC ECOSYSTEM: EMBRACING DYNAMIC CHANGE FOR THE NEXT GENERATION OF ARTISTS AND MUSIC FANS

Frank Briegmann, CEO of UNIVERSAL MUSIC Germany and President Central Europe of UNIVERSAL MUSIC GROUP, talks about the digital transformation that the music industry is going through. As a result of this disruption, music fans can use today a much broader variety of platforms and formats than in the past.
Consequences of this transformation are on one side the increased importance of the role that the music company plays in areas like marketing or A&R and on the other side the threaten of the value gap that can't be resolved without a new legislation.

snippet.title: A European Single Market for Citizens and Philanthropy (Felix Oldenburg) | DLDeurope 16
snippet.description: Goods and services can move freely across borders in Europe. So do social challenges. Solving them outside national borders, however, is crippled by national norms and regulations. Felix outlines a timely vision for a Europe that tears down the barriers for charity and philanthropy, and allows every citizen to help tackle social problems wherever they are.

snippet.title: Protecting Europe's Personal Data (John Frank, Microsoft & Natalia Drozdiak, WSJ) | DLDeurope 16
snippet.description: In recent months there has been progress when it comes to protecting the privacy rights of citizens across Europe. The EU agreed on a new and strong data protection regulation, the Privacy Shield was adopted after extensive and rigorous debate and the latest decision in the Microsoft warrant case is a milestone for ensuring that European citizens’ privacy rights are protected by their own laws. But important questions remain such as how do we balance governments’ legitimate interest to keep the public safe while protecting citizens’ fundamental rights? How do we preserve digital sovereignty while and improving cross-border cooperation and advancing international frameworks to avoid conflicts of laws?

snippet.title: DLDeurope 2016 Highlights | DLDeurope
BREXIT Contagion? (S.Adams, T.Hunt, S.Shakespeare, C.Grobe, A.Achleitner) | DLDeurope 16
snippet.description:
BREXIT CONTAGION? THE POLITICAL FALLOUT FOR EUROPE AND ITS TECHNOLOGY SECTOR

In collaboration with the Global Counsel.

Britain’s vote to leave the European Union is a landmark reversal in the history of European integration and arguably the most significant economic demerger between major western economies since the Second World War – one that risks disrupting the movement of goods, services and people between the UK and the rest of the EU. This session will outline the risks of Brexit contagion for the rest of Europe and will focus particularly on the future of the tech and media sectors both in the UK and the remaining EU.

The panel will be hosted by Stephen Adams, partner at Global Counsel, and will feature Stephan Shakespeare, founder and CEO of the British online market research and opinion polling company YouGov, who will explain the demographics behind the Brexit vote and the implications for eurosceptic parties in other EU countries; Professor Ann-Kristin Achleitner, Chair of Entrepreneurial Finance at the Technische Universität München (TUM), who will outline the financial risks posed by the UK’s exit, particularly for the EU start-ups, and suggest possible remedies that could boost entrepreneurial culture; Christian Grobe, co-founder and COO of the online lending marketplace FundingCircle Continental Europe, who will assess whether Brexit could prompt a flight from London to new and rising European tech-hubs, such as Berlin, Dublin and Stockholm; and Tristram Hunt, a British Member of Parliament and senior lecturer at Queen Mary, University of London, who will assess the current upsurge of political populism from a historical perspective.

snippet.title: The Microbiome (Berndt Birkner, Founder of the Gastroenterology at Max Weber Place) | DLDsummer 16
snippet.description:
The human microbiome is composed of trillions of bacteria, viruses and fungi. These microbes reside in and on our whole body e.g. the oropharyngeal space, the urogenital organs, the skin and the gut, mainly. The human microbiome has tremendous potential to impact our physiology, both in health and disease. Great advances in studying the human microbiome were made possible through culture-independent analyses. The bacterial constituents were identified through 16 S RNA sequenzing thereby formulating the human metagenome, which is more than 100 fold greater than the human genome.

Diversity, richness and abundance of the microbes are important characteristics of the human microbiome for his functions as a friend or foe. The human microbiome forms with his microbes an active biofilm on the human surfaces protecting or eroding the underlying mucosa.

Moreover the human microbiome is a highly active metabolite producer , the metabolome. In combination with environmental, nutritional, pharmacologic or genetic host factors the human metabolome induces an inflammatory response and blocks intended pharmaceutical therapies.

A number of different metabolic diseases e.g. diabetes, obesity, fatty liver or cardiovascular diseases are presumably caused by the malfunction, known as dysbiosis, of the Human microbiome. The human microbiome is connected via the brain-gut axis with the human brain inducing mood disturbances and mental diseases.

Scientific research studying probiotics, prebiotics and antibiotics is under way to elucidate the therapeutic possibilities of the abovementioned diseases. Moreover the human fecal microbiota transplantation is established as an accepted indication for the refractory clostridium difficile infection of the colon.

Future research studies will produce more insights in the function and malfunction of the human microbiome.

snippet.title: Throwing Rocks At The Google Bus (Douglas Rushkoff, CUNY/Queens & Andrian Kreye) | DLDnyc 16
snippet.description:
A story that started 1000 years ago about how growth became the enemy of prosperity. Throwing Rocks at the Google Bus is the newest book of Douglas Rushkoff and it relates why the digital economy has gone wrong. Everybody knows it, but no one knows quite how to fix it, or even how to explain the problem. Workers lose to automation, investors lose to algorithms, musicians lose to power law dynamics, drivers lose to Uber, neighborhoods lose to Airbnb, and even tech developers lose their visions to the demands of the startup economy.

Douglas Rushkoff argues that it doesn’t have to be this way. This isn’t the fault of digital technology at all, but the way we are deploying it: instead of building the distributed digital economy these new networks could foster, we are doubling down on the industrial age mandate for growth above all. As Rushkoff shows, this is more the legacy of early corporatism and central currency than a feature of digital technology.

snippet.title: How Bots Can Make Life Better (Dennis Mortensen, Joshua Browder, Nicholas Thompson) | DLDnyc 16
snippet.description:
A robot lawyer that provides free legal help in under 30 seconds or and a personal assistant who schedules meetings for you are just two examples of how bots can make our lifes better or at least, easier.

snippet.title: Audience, Relevance And Context – The Future Of PR And Marketing (Richard Edelman) | DLDnyc 16
snippet.description:
This panel is about the rapid evolution of the PR industry and the need to re-invent marketing. 
The best brands now earn the right to be partners in consumers’ lives, moving beyond selling toward trusted relationships. The company must recognize social and societal trends to evolve its products.
The ad agencies envisage a time when advertising is served up for each customer based on prior search history and knowledge of transactions. The important elements are Audience, Relevance and Context. Reaching consumers at the right time and right place is critical. This is especially so because of the game changing power of the mobile device. More hours per day are spent on the cell phone than any other medium. Mobile is both a channel and a context.
The equal partner in marketing must be public relations. The major aspects of modern PR are Buzz, Trend and Context. There is a difference between attention grabbing and persuasion. So where does the PR industry go in the next decade?

snippet.title: Networks vs. Hierarchies: A Delicate Relationship (Niall Ferguson, Professor at Harvard) | DLD16
snippet.description: Niall Ferguson, a Professor of History at Harvard University, will talk about how interactions between hierarchies and networks affect innovation. He argues that the horizontally-organized networks are spontaneously self-organizing, which fosters creativity and innovation. Hierarchies, in contrast, are vertically and less spontaneously organized, which is why they seek to exploit the positive externalities of networks. A functioning, progressive society depends on those networks. However, if hierarchies start to control the networks to the extent that their self-organizing properties are lost, innovation will slow down. This trade-off has been observed throughout history, and Mr. Ferguson will discuss how it applies today.

snippet.title: Unmasking Achilles: Today's Wars & Devastations (Jody Williams, Nobel Prize & Ralph Simon) | DLD16
snippet.description: While today some contend that wars are on the decline, Sudan, Afghanistan and other parts of the world would consider anyone making such claims completely mad. And the countries and people facing the blowback of these wars on their own doorsteps would likely agree with them. In order to deal with the rapid, mass movements of people fleeing war and seeking refuge, we must delve deeply inside ourselves and be willing to go to the root causes of such movement. We must unmask the heroic image of the Achilles-type warrior and reveal the reality of war and all its consequences. In the globalized world, everything affects everything and the ripple effects touch us all in one way or another. The ultimate answer to the above questions is confronting and stopping the endless cycles of conflict. It is not a short-term solution but the situation in which we find ourselves today did not happen overnight either.

snippet.title: Exponential Space Technology: Getting Weather Right (Theresa Condor, Spire Global) | DLD16
snippet.description: The economic losses of extreme or uncertain weather-events are distributed across every industry and every country around the world, and are increasing in impact as climate change disrupts what we thought we knew about seasonal norms. Yet, our ability to accurately predict the weather, even in the short-term, remains frustratingly inadequate. The industry throws out words like Big Data, Supercomputing, and AI to explain the complexity problem, with the bar for improvement set at 1 day of forecasting gain per decade. Spire, a satellite-powered data company, is changing this by providing data that will result in a step function change in weather forecasting accuracy. It is both new technologies and a new mindset that is driving Spire’s progress in barely three years from the archetypal San Francisco start-up garage to an operational satellite constellation for high volume, high impact weather data that will allow us to finally get weather right, and to then make the decisions that save lives, infrastructure, and money.

snippet.title: The Golden Age of Storytelling (Julian Morris, Dan Lyons, Martin Moszkowicz, Ralph Simon) | DLD16

What exactly is going to change for the directors, the screenplay writers, actors and costume designers? Julian Morris (actor) argues that we are in a “golden age of television” and likely to see similarly positive developments in film, too. What does he mean when talking about a “golden age”? Are there negative effects too?
