snippet.title: Urban Metagenomics (Kevin Slavin, Professor at MIT Media Lab) | DLD16
snippet.description: The human body is made up not only of the „human“ multi-cell organisms, but also of a variety of single-cell organisms. The various organisms that live in and on the human body make up the human microbiome. As a result, each one of us is essentially a superorganism, with life inside and on us that keeps us healthy, can make us sick, and may well be at the root of so much of our overall health. Scientific advances have made it possible to research microbes previously invisible to us. Microbes have different origins, but the majority is propagated through what we touch and breathe. Consequently, four different research groups in the US have committed their research to the urban microbiome. They are interested in learning more about whether microbial communities differ across urban landscapes, and how this might affect human health in invisible, powerful and surprising ways.

snippet.title: Blockchain: "It's Going to Radically Transform Our Society's Institutions" (Don Tapscott) | DLD16
snippet.description: Don Tapscott, a leading theorist of the digital age, explains why the blockchain technology will fundamentally transform the institutions our societies are built upon. Because the blockchain technology powers the digital currency Bitcoin, it will not only affect how business is being made, but also our legal systems. Ultimately, the effect of the blockchain technology will be much more farreaching; it will also transform governance, healthcare, education, and various other pillars of our societies.

snippet.title: Longevity & Lifestyle (Lisa Mosconi, NYU School of Medicine) | DLD16
snippet.description: Dr. Lisa Mosconi, founder and director of the Nutrition & Brain Fitness Lab at the NYU School of Medicine, will give a talk on the role of nature (genes) versus nurture (lifestyles), and specifically on whether and, if so, how positive dietary choices can reduce the risk of dementia. Dr. Mosconi explains that despite an increase in life expectancy, we are “facing a brain health crisis”. She argues that because the brain changes leading to dementia, for example, unfold over a 20 to 40 year time span, there is a precious window of time. Preventive strategies, such as lifestyle adjustments, during this crucial timespan may well make disease modification possible. Dr. Mosconi considers diet and nutrition to play a particularly important role in this.

snippet.description: Leila Janah and Felix Oldenburg will pick up where previous panels on the future of work have left off and discuss the changes we are facing in our work life. A relevant question is whether the social consequences of changes in the job market should be overseen and balanced out by socially-oriented businesses, or whether we need stronger political regulations and frameworks. Leila Janah is the CEO of Samasource, a company that seeks to enable the provision of equal opportunities for all people when it comes to access to education, work and health care. snippet.title: Design and the Life Sciences (Daisy Ginsberg, Michael John Gorman, Paola Antonelli) | DLD16
snippet.description: The intersection of design and synthetic biology is a powerful new direction of research and practice. Four early advocates and pioneers of what Ginsberg calls the Synthetic Kingdom – a new branch in the Tree of Life – will discuss it from the unique viewpoint of their respective fields. From early efforts to establish synthetic biology as a new area of inquiry in academia, to early experiments in the design of a connection with art and design across many universities and institutions around the world – Alexandra Daisy Ginsberg, Michael John Gorman will engage in an inspiring conversation, moderated by Paola Antonelli.

snippet.description: Rohan Silva, the co-founder of Second Home, a place where entrepreneurs and businesses come together, will talk about the impact of the built environment on creativity, wellbeing and entrepreneurship. In a colorful talk, using images and slides, Rohan Silva wants to investigate how the places we work (and live) in can support inter-disciplinary thinking and behavior – by sparking serendipitous collisions, and bringing together diverse industries, people and ideas. Rohan Silva will also make an exciting announcement at DLD16.

snippet.title: Propaganda in the Internet Age (Daniel van der Velden, Metahaven & Christy Lange, Frieze) | DLD16
snippet.description:
What does propaganda in the Internet age look like? Daniel van der Velden will show footage from Metahaven's debut feature film The Sprawl. In an interview with Christy Lange, he gives insights into the film’s trajectory and explains how Metahaven uses graphic design, identity branding, and product development as a means to investigate existing commercial and political power structures.


The Sprawl is an immersive video installation that explores the mutation of propaganda in the age of social media. The project investigates the recent Ebola outbreak, the conflict between Ukraine and Russia, and the rise of the Islamic State (ISIS) through the internet and traditional news media. Unlike previous eras, where the state continuously enforces one propagandistic message to the public, the example of these three crises reveals how propaganda now exists within a horizontal field of instant, multiple messages.

snippet.title: Transience (Michael Craig-Martin & Hans Ulrich Obrist, Serpentine Gallery) | DLD16
snippet.description: Michael Craig-Martin is an important contemporary conceptual artist whose exhibition Transience is currently shown at the Serpentine Galleries in London. The exhibition exposes the visitor to how the world has changed over the past 30 years. The exhibition features paintings of mundane technological objects, such as batteries, light bulbs, or cassettes, depicted in saturated colors – some of them created with the help of a software algorithm. In a previous public talk, Michael Craig-Martin and Hans Ulrich Obrist discussed Craig-Martin’s practice and the transformations in design and technology.

In a way, the journey that mobile gaming has been on for the past five years is a very interesting example of how quickly transformation works nowadays, and how important timing is, from immature playground, to ultra-competitive sector. snippet.description: A discussion with real-world examples on how the Age of Intelligence is transforming the way we live, work, and play.

snippet.title: Navigating the Stream (Lutz Schüler, Jon Steinberg, Jared Grusd, David Kirkpatrick) | DLD16
snippet.description: Following up on the two previous sessions about media and TV networks, this panel will provide the audience with food for thought on a range of related topics. The panel discussion between Lutz Schüler, Jon Steinberg, and Jared Grusd will be moderated by David Kirkpatrick. Topics to be discussed include: shifts in the media landscape, how to find the right content in a time of oversupply, how to attract millennials, quality content and live news versus user generated “clickbait”, and new business models.

snippet.title: Follow Me - The Home Entertainment Robot (Pierre Lebeau, Founder and CEO at Keecker) | DLD16
snippet.description: Keecker is the world’s first HomePod – a Home Entertainment Robot, capable of moving around on its own, or as instructed by an app-based remote, and transforming any wall, door or ceiling into a huge projected screen. Pierre Lebeau, the founder of Keecker and former Product Manager of Google, seeks to reshape home technology. Keecker can act as a digital entertainment center for video, music, photos, web browsing, and gaming. Users will also be able to take advantage of its big screen for working on documents, staying up to date on all matters social, or just checking emails and newsfeeds.

snippet.title: Projects with Music (Michele de Lucchi) | DLD16
snippet.description: This panel will address the interface of design and digitalization. The digital revolution has an immense effect on design, creating new tools to conceive, to design, to visualize, and come up with new ideas in the fields of architecture and design. The ability to merge design projects with music, for instance, increases the emotional value of these projects and thus adds to the overall message the designer seeks to bring across.

snippet.title: Data Drives Business (Carlo Ratti, Thorsten Dirks, Antoine Blondeau, Marc Bergen) | DLD16
snippet.description: The panelists will explore ways of streamlining businesses through the use of data, and, conversely, the possibilities of using data to create new providers, which strive for full data transparency and the right of “non-disclosure”, enabling real “digital self-determination” for the customer. What are sensible ways to use the ever-increasing amount of data? How do we turn “big data” into “smart data”, while ensuring the rights of consumers?

snippet.title: Design's Trilogy: Creativity, Tradition, Innovation (Lapo Elkann, Sam Handy, Yana Peel) | DLD16
snippet.description: In this session, two creative visionaries will come together to discuss individual projects, along with their hybrid collaboration that is re-defining the rules of fashion, and breaking the boundaries of design. Lapo Elkann and Sam Handy have managed to maintain their independence, while bringing authenticity to their companies’ core concepts. Both recognize the importance of heritage, while, simultaneously, venturing into the future of design. Elkann and Handy have been able to harness new technologies and ideas, leading to intelligent, thoughtful, and creative designs. As the title suggests, this panel will address the three keys to design: creativity, tradition, and innovation.

snippet.description: Dominik Wee and Jennifer Dungs will discuss the future of mobility. In a conversation hosted by Mathias Müller von Blumencron, they will assess the promises as well as the challenges (increasing software complexities, and security risks) we will encounter while moving into the next age of mobility. What will the future automobiles look like? What advantages would an iCar have? Will some OEM’s build their full stack of technology on their own?

snippet.title: Narratives and Business (John Hagel, Deloitte) | DLD16
snippet.description: Most of us understand the great power of stories in connecting with people, but we tend to overlook the even greater power of narratives in mobilizing people and building deep loyalty. This talk will explore the key distinctions between stories and narratives and explore why these distinctions matter. Narratives play a key role at multiple levels – personal, institutional and social – but this talk will focus on the missed opportunities for institutions to harness the power of narrative. In particular, it will suggest that the companies creating the most value in the future will be those that develop narratives that become the foundation for movements. In a world where attention is becoming a scarcer resource, narratives hold the key to not only attract, but hold the attention of a growing number of people.

snippet.title: Our Secret to Innovation (Werner Vogels at Amazon, Christopher Schläffer, Stefan Winners) | DLD16
snippet.description: In this panel, Werner Vogels, from Amazon, and Christopher Schläffer, from Vimpelcom, will talk about innovating businesses in the Information Age. Potential topics include: What is Amazon’s secret to innovation, and how can it serve as a model for other firms? What is the role of values and culture in innovation? Does fundamentally re-building a business have a different innovation effect than adapting to new challenges step-by-step? Which path was taken by Amazon and Vimpelcom? This session will highlight what innovation means and how it can be championed within a global organization. It will debate whether businesses innovating under pressure all use common drivers for innovation.

snippet.title: Hosting the World (Nathan Blecharczyk, CTO and Co-Founder at Airbnb & David Rowan) | DLD16
snippet.description: Together, Nathan Blecharczyk and David Rowan will explore the underlying principles of the “sharing economy”, in general, and the global growth of home sharing, in particular. Europe is embracing the sharing economy, a part of which – home sharing – has already become common practice. How do innovations like these benefit travelers worldwide? AirBnB, for example, allows for authentic travel experiences, and connects communities and cities across the world.

snippet.title: Augmenting Reading (Chris Nicholas, President at Asymmetrica Labs) | DLD16
snippet.description: Asymmetrica has created a format, called Asym, which will make web user experiences more enjoyable. Two of the main things reducing the value of the web are illiteracy and distractions. Asym seeks to overcome both through micro-typographic formatting. Changing the word spacing (some spaces are large, others smaller) in web texts encourages effective eye movement, thus improving cognition. Asym is currently available in English and Spanish. The German version will be launched exclusively at DLD16, while running a live demo of Asym to show how micro-typographic text reformatting works.

snippet.title: Click & Watch II (Robert Kyncl, CBO at YouTube & Yossi Vardi) | DLD16
snippet.description: Robert Kyncl, in conversation with Yossi Vardi, will discuss the changing media landscape and the movement away from linear TV towards on-demand, digital videos. At a time where we are increasingly facing and over-supply of content, how can YouTube help other brands to stand out? What roles do partnerships (for example with Go Pro) play in this? How will virtual reality change our viewing behavior, and consequently the platforms we chose? What is the new YouTube Red subscription going to change, also with regards to online visual content? How does YouTube stand out among other online TV networks? What is the secret?

snippet.title: Click & Watch I (Reed Hastings, CEO at Netflix & Claus Kleber, ZDF) | DLD16
snippet.description: Global Internet TV networks, with Netflix being the most prominent example, will be at the center of this conversation between Reed Hastings (Netflix) and Claus Kleber. Questions to be discussed will include: How does one set up a global Internet TV network, and which challenges are involved? What about personalization and data? What role do partnerships play in this? How can we expect content to change, and what are the next steps for Netflix with regards to content?

snippet.title: Why We Believe in Quality Content (Altchek, B.Lo, A.Klöpping, M.Burger-Calderon, A.Zielina) | DLD16
snippet.description:
This panel deals with strategic approaches on how to build valuable media and online content at a time where consumption behavior is changing. People increasingly consume visual and written content (including news) from the same websites/apps. As more things compete for the limited time of consumers –often resulting in an information overload – it gets harder for content companies to reach their audience. Connected issues that will also be discussed here include: How do we create an intelligent mobile experience? How can we monetize content? What is the role of mobile advertising?
Panel at DLD by Miguel Burger-Calderon, Chris Altchek, Alexander Klöpping and Bobby Lo. Moderated by Anita Zielina.

snippet.title: Innovation and Entrepreneurship in Europe (N.Kolev, N.Kroes, K.Speck, F.Talpes, J.Schenker) | DLD16
snippet.description: Several of the panelists for this session come from places that don't immediately spring to mind as digital hotspots but are gaining recognition for tech strengths: Amsterdam, Bucharest and Karlsruhe. This panel will address the growing digital market in Europe, and elaborate on why it is important for cities and regions in Europe that want to be known for their tech strengths to market themselves accordingly. Neelie Kroes, who helped set the digital agenda for Europe, will also touch on some of the issues that still need resolving in order to truly support the entrepreneurial spirit in Europe, including getting corporates to work more closely with start-ups.

snippet.title: How Will Publishers Survive? (Robert Thomson, CEO at NewsCorp & Zanny Minton-Beddoes) | DLD16
snippet.description: Zanny Minton-Beddoes and Robert Thomson will discuss the future of publishing, not only with regards to magazine or newspapers, but also books. How will print-media (and online media) change in the face of increasing digitalization? What are the challenges, what the opportunities? Robert Thomson is a big Google critic who considers online-media sources to be predators for conventional print news sources – an interesting departure point for fruitful discussion.

snippet.title: How Will Journalism Survive? (M.Al-Hames, Z.Minton-Beddoes, N.Pearlstine, Ken Auletta) | DLD16
snippet.description: This panel discussion, moderated by Ken Auletta, will investigate the future of journalism in light of the increasing digitalization of our society. Together, the panelists will also address the nature of big media companies: how do they evolve? How do they act on the market? Is digitalization favoring the creation of new media groups, or do the “old” ones simply have to adapt – and if so, how?

snippet.title: Romanian Startup Champions (Vlad Ciurca & Oana Petrus, Techsylvania) | DLD16
snippet.description: During this informal breakfast and networking session, five Romanian startups will introduce their products and ideas. Romania is home to a flourishing startup scene, resulting in many interesting and creative products. The startups that will be introduced during this DLD16 session are: Symme 3D, a company building 3D printers; Moqups, who designs tools for project managers; SkinVision, who developed an app that allows people to keep track of their moles, and understand personal risk for melanoma skin cancer; Airivision, creators of an Evolutionary Artificial Intelligence computing vision engine; and Jellycs/Transylgamia, one of Romania’s biggest gaming studios.

snippet.title: A Tailored Album (Beatie Wolfe) | DLD16
snippet.description: Beatie Wolfe will be telling the story of her Musical Jacket, cut by the tailors of Hendrix and Bowie out of fabric woven with the geometric patterns of Beatie’s single, recorded in the room where McCartney wrote “Eleanor Rigby” and Hendrix penned “The Wind Cries Mary”. This is the story of a truly tailored album release for the 21st Century. Beatie Wolfe will also perform live.

snippet.title: On Life in the Infosphere (Jacob Burda, Luciano Floridi, P.Weibel, P.Sloterdijk, J.Jarvis) | DLD16
snippet.description: Prior to the panel discussion between Peter Sloterdijk and Peter Weibel, Luciano Floridi will give a keynote speech. Floridi will discuss the rise of the infosphere and how it is transforming our economies. He will also look at these questions from an ethical perspective. Sloterdijk will propose an explanation of the digital infosphere using three distinct spheres outlined in his books. Weibel, coming from the arts and sciences, highlights the novelty of transforming data into things, made possible only by the digital revolution. This panel discussion seeks to shed light on the yet little understood spheres of digital transformation and life in the infosphere. If we want to truly be in control of the changes we are observing right now, a thorough understanding of the underlying processes becomes imperative.

snippet.title: Beyond Business: The Responsibility of Global Players (Joanna Shields, UK Government) | DLD16
snippet.description: Joanna Shields will start the panel with discussing the growing responsibility of businesses to make digital progress compatible with national laws, and establish sensitivity for the needs of society, including data security. The panelists will further elaborate on incompatibilities between national laws and the politics of businesses, while also venturing into potential solutions to this.

snippet.description:
“The airplane became the first world wide web”, as Bill Gates once said. Today, IT and Industry are virtually converging. But what does that really mean for aerospace? And how are companies in this sector concretely coping with new chances, challenges and competitors?


Together with Rebecca Blumenstein, Deputy Editor in Chief of Wall Street Journal, Airbus Group CEO Tom Enders will shed a light on these questions and unveil the Group´s latest digital initiatives in Silicon Valley and beyond.

snippet.title: The Third Industrial Revolution and a Zero Marginal Cost Society (Jeremy Rifkin) | DLD16
snippet.description: Jeremy Rifkin will lay out a “Game plan for the future”, referring to the advent of a smart green digital economy as part of the Third Industrial Revolution. Rifkin argues that we are about to experience fundamental changes to our societies and economies, as a result of the digitalization of communication, energy, and transportation. Together, a digitalized communication Internet, a digitalized renewable energy Internet, and a digitalized automated Transportation and Logistics Internet, will create a super-Internet of Things infrastructure. This Internet of Things infrastructure will have to be scaled up and supported in order to enable the transition to a Third Industrial Revolution. Rifkin considers the European Union and China leaders in this quest for change. He highlights, in particular, the economic and social opportunities that could arise from such a transition.

snippet.title: AI: Big Expectations (Jürgen Schmidhuber, President at IDSIA) | DLD16
snippet.description: Jürgen Schmidhuber will provide a comprehensive framework for thinking about artificial intelligence (AI). He will review past developments in artificial intelligence, and discuss its current (and expected future) effect on the work life, various industries, and infrastructure and traffic design.

snippet.title: Power to the European Founders (Niklas Zennström, Founder and CEO at Atomico & Murad Ahmed) | DLD16
snippet.description: By co-founding Skype, Europe’s first billion dollar tech company, at a time where most great digital innovations came from the Silicon Valley, Niklas Zennström proved Europe’s ability to grow the next wave of billion dollar companies. He believes that technical expertise should be more widely shared in order to truly realize Europe’s potential of becoming the home of many more companies alike. He will be joined onstage by Murad Ahmed, The Financial Times’ European Technology Correspondent.

snippet.title: Marketplace Europe: EU's Digital Landscape (Stein, Samwer, Stoppelman, Jens Spahn, Mettler) | DLD16
snippet.description: The panelists will elaborate on the key issues introduced in Margrethe Vestager’s keynote. In a panel discussion, moderated by Ann Mettler, they will discuss the tensions that arise when trying to make innovation and data security compatible. How can data analysis lead to the creation of new businesses? What role does the consumer play, and to what extent are the regulatory frameworks that are in place sufficient? How will digital technologies change the European economic landscape? Does Europe have the edge over other markets with its long-standing engineering expertise? Or does software know-how reign supreme? All of these questions will make for an interesting debate on the future of the “marketplace Europe”.

snippet.description: In her keynote speech, Margrethe Vestager will discuss Europe’s vision for a digital future; highlight the importance of fostering partnerships between entrepreneurs and politics, and keeping markets open and competitive; while also talking about uniform rules for businesses in Europe.

snippet.title: Stem Cells: The Future of Medicine (Eckhard Alt, Isar Klinikum) | DLDsummer 15
snippet.description:
Over the past 50 years, there has been great progress in medicine primarily due to the use of artificial implants restoring compromised body functions. The next generation of medicine will be to better understand the healing power and the repair mechanisms which are intrinsic to our body based on stem cells. Research over the last years has revealed that stem cells are distributed throughout the whole body as they are located in every blood vessel. Each organ has its own stem cell pool which serves as its primary regenerative source. However the use of these “repair cells” is confined to the respective organ. Future stem cell therapy will be based on the possibility to retrieve stem cells from an organ that is not compromised by the removal of a part of its stem cell pool, to separate and concentrate these cells, and to inject them into a target organ or site of the body in need of repair. The primary source of these naturally pluripotent stem cells are the small blood vessels located within the adipose tissue as the impact of removal of tissue on the site of recovery typically is low. The number of stem cells to be found in the adipose tissue, when an adequate recovery and processing method is applied, is in a range of nearly one million cells per gram tissue, which is many fold higher than for cells found in the bone marrow. Current experience and results from clinical treatment with pluripotent stem cells has shown a very high safety profile and remarkable results in treating various diseases, such as orthopedic conditions, skin repair non-healing wounds and other diseases.

snippet.description:
The future of healthcare is about "better" not just "more." More data, more devices, and more drugs may help, but alone they won’t make us healthier. Better health requires becoming smarter about getting what we really need, when we really need it. In a future enriched by multiple forms of computing (from tablets, to smartphones, to wearables, and even digestible and implantable devices), the key to better understanding our health and optimizing our lives will be personalized feedback tailored to each individual and delivered via seamless digital channels that themselves collect and transmit data. The great secret that will turn frustrating "episodes" with the healthcare system into a positive end-to-end "healthcare experience” is data-driven guidance and immediate access to care. Anytime, anywhere access to doctor insights (information) and care (consultations), guided by personal data, will create, for the first time ever, an entirely new experience in health: access to the right care at the right time in the right place at the right price, enabling us to feel better every day and live longer healthier happier lives.

William Zhou is the co-founder and CEO of Chalk.com, an education software company focused in K-12. Zhou has been passionate about entrepreneurship from a young age, founding his first company in high school. He launched his first Internet business in 2010, which he sold at the age 18 during his first year of computer science at the University of Waterloo. To pursue the bigger challenge of changing education, Zhou founded Chalk.com to create a productivity suite for K-12 teachers. Forbes recently named Zhou top 30 under 30. Today, Chalk.com is used in over 20,000 and Chalk.com is empowering teachers to focus on what matters most - their students.

snippet.title: Interview with Andrea Accomazzo (European Space Ag Agency, ESA) | DLD15
snippet.description:
Italian, born 1970.
After high school started at the Academy of the Italian Air Force and completed the basic training as a military pilot from 1989 till 1991.
Continued engineering studies at the Politecnico di Milano, graduated in Aerospace Engineering in 1995.
Worked at Fiat Avio from 1995 till 1999, mainly for the Vega launch vehicle and the Rosetta lander.
Joined ESA in 1999 as Rosetta operations engineer at ESOC.
After having launched Rosetta in 2004, nominated as Spacecraft Operations Manager for Venus Express, launched in 2005 and inserted in Venus orbit in 2006.
At the end of 2006 returned to Rosetta as Spacecraft Operations Manager, a role that he kept till earlier this year after Rosetta completed the hibernation phase.
Since 2013, Head of the Solar and Planetary Missions Division in the Mission Operations Department at ESOC.
As such also the Ground Segment Manager for all missions in development (Bepi Colombo, Solar Orbiter, Juice, Exomars) and the Flight Director for Rosetta.
(He likes playing football, mountain-biking, mountaineering and skiing).

snippet.title: Seeing Differently: Filling the Space between the Real and Digital (Beau Lotto, Ripple Inc) | DLD15
snippet.description:
Smartphones have become an integral part of our daily lives. Messaging apps enable us to keep in touch with our dear ones round the clock. UCL neuroscientist Beau Lotto however argues that these apps cause our brains to inhabit our phones and foster a level of anxiety.

He speaks about his new messaging app, called Traces, which lets its users leave messages behind at certain geographic locations. Recipients can only discover those messages by traveling to the same location, which according to Beau Lotto adds more value and manifests a messaging experience at a fundamental level.

snippet.description:

OpenStreetMap, microsatellites, open source, drones, crowdsourcing are completely changing the landscape and are introducing a kind of "neogeography". snippet.title: Is the CMO the New CTO (Michael Mendenhall, Lynn Vojvodich, Wes Nichols, Eric Hippeau) | DLD15
snippet.description:
Marketers spend over $1 trillion annually to reach consumers worldwide. They play a crucial role in the modern economy. For decades, the marketing tools have been relatively stable and predictable: television, print, market research, merchandising, promotions, events and more. In recent years, technology has disrupted the marketing world like never before: web, digital media, streaming, social networks, mobile, messaging, programmatic, sponsored content, viral videos. A never-ending stream of new technology is being offered to marketers in a dizzying array of new platforms, devices, networks and content forms. Suddenly, the Chief Marketing Officers is buying more technology than their colleagues in the traditional Information Technology functions.

Are CMOs prepared for this dramatic change? Will their traditional network of agency consultants survive the tech onslaught? Should they be given the responsibility to develop the company’s consumer-facing applications and services? Should they become a publisher to feed to constant need for content in social media? Should the CMO become the CCO: the Chief CONSUMER Officer?

Intro & moderation by Eric Hippeau

Her books have been translated into more than forty languages.

According to Ann-Kristin Achleitner and Antonella Mei-Pochtler there is need for a change in the human resource management of businesses. The deficiency of German business formations is often deplored nowadays. Besides the frequently mentioned weak funding possibilities there is another reason which is often neglected: the opportunity costs at the labor market. The rigid system should be renewed to enable an easier access for lateral entrants. Ann-Kristin Achleitner supports a personnel turnover between companies and company founder. The entry-level conditions for employees are akin to the Bermuda triangle. There´s a need for rotation!

snippet.title: DLDwomen14 - 21st Century Branding - From Heritage to Digital (Phair, Duma, Missoni)
snippet.description:

President of THE OUTNET.COM, Stephanie Phair has helped redefine the online shopping landscape, and in particular, how designer brands can be presented on a discount site in a way that maintains their luxe look and feel. Brand ambassador, Margherita Missoni successfully communicates the uniqueness and heritage of the traditional Maison Missoni. Miroslava Duma has become a mega brand herself and delivers lifestyle and fashion content via her site Buro 24/7. Unique approaches that have one common objective: Building strong brands!

snippet.title: DLDwomen14 - Qualify for the Future: Does Digitalization Make the World a Better Place?
snippet.description:
Companies and Authorities are overfilled of personal data. They create personality patterns and seem to know people better than themselves. Cornelia Quennet-Thielen and Stefanie Wahl ponder the challenges, possibilities and risks of digitalization and data pooling. On the one side new individual, economic and societal possibilities are created. On the other side a safety gap open. How do we want to live in times of Industry 4.0? How can we handle the future of work, education and safety? Probably politics shouldn´t sort out all these affairs its own.

snippet.title: DLD NYC 14 - Beauty of Failure (Don Dodge, Pat Mitchell)
snippet.description:
It is a popular myth that all good ideas and products are miraculously developed at exactly the right time -- just when they were needed and the market was ready for them. In a lot of cases, quite the opposite is true: the best results were born from a series of failures or from taking big risks. However, nobody wants to be associated with failure -- especially in business.

Don Dodge and Pat Mitchell will talk about how important it is to embrace failure -- since it is only by setting audacious goals, and thinking outside the box about how to achieve them, that truly revolutionary breakthroughs can be achieved.

snippet.title: How to Train Your Mind and Your Heart (Tania Singer, Max Planck Institute) | DLD14
snippet.description:
A world expert on empathy, Tania Singer explores how improved cognitive and mental skills foster stability of mind, open hearts and encourage cooperation. After a short talk on the neurobiological basis of compassion, she'll leads a special DLD workshop based on her freely downloadable multi-media eBook "Compassion. Bridging Science and Practice." Developed through a cooperative effort of neuroscientists, therapists, contemplative scholars and monks, the book describes a variety of secular mental training programs, their use in education, clinical settings and for everyday life, as well as scientific findings on the resulting changes of brain, health and general well-being.

She'll also present the ReSource Project, a unique one-year program blending Eastern and Western methods of mental training. Over a period of nine months, 200 participants practice exercises designed to enhance attentional control, body- and self-awareness, healthy emotion regulation, self-care, compassion, empathy, and perspective-taking. Participants meditate each day, attend weekly sessions with teachers and are tested at regular intervals. The aim of the training is to improve mental health and clarity, reduce stress and increase understanding of others' views, values and actions.

snippet.description:

Ask about artificial intelligence and science fiction often comes to mind. But back in the real world, computers that act independently, make autonomous decisions and learn from their mistakes now sit very literally in everyone's pocket--courtesy simultaneous revolutions in mobility, big data & cloud computing. From serving ads and making investments to diagnosing disease and driving cars, AI is making itself indispensable--and raising questions that can no longer be avoided. What does it mean for a machine to be intelligent? Will computers increasingly replace humans or merely augment them? How will our legal and cultural frameworks accommodate autonomous devices? And could there be a "singularity," with computers exceeding human understanding and taking real control?

snippet.title: Digital Storytelling: Surfing the Video Explosion (Schulz,Edwards,Maymann,Rafati,Blodget) | DLD14
snippet.description:
Introduction by Henry Blodget (Business Insider).

Multiplying platforms, broadband wireless, social networks and real-time streaming--the medium formerly known as television is ground zero for every new digital wave. For viewers, it's an age of amazing abundance, from millions of short-form videos to the latest Hollywood epic on demand. For content owners and distributors, it's an endless battle to keep up--with old rivals and disruptive new competitors alike. Is a new business landscape for visual media finally coming into focus? Will digital-native kids, dedicated mobile apps and binge-viewers increasingly drive not just what we watch, but the ways we watch it? Is technology redrawing the lines between movies and TV--and between paid and "free"?

With Stefan Schulz (Watchever), Jamal Edwards (sb.tv), Jimmy Maymann (The Huffington Post), Shahrzad Rafati (BroadbandTV) and moderated by Henry Blodget (Business Insider).

snippet.title: Predictive Computing: A.I. Gets Real (G.John, M.Saxena, B.Medlock, W.Vogels, S.Patterson) | DLD14
snippet.description:
A panel with: George John, Manoj Saxena, Ben Medlock and Werner Vogels.
Moderated by: Simon Patterson, Silver Lake.

Ask about artificial intelligence and science fiction often comes to mind. But back in the real world, computers that act independently, make autonomous decisions and learn from their mistakes now sit very literally in everyone's pocket--courtesy simultaneous revolutions in mobility, big data & cloud computing. From serving ads and making investments to diagnosing disease and driving cars, AI is making itself indispensable--and raising questions that can no longer be avoided. What does it mean for a machine to be intelligent? Will computers increasingly replace humans or merely augment them? How will our legal and cultural frameworks accommodate autonomous devices? And could there be a "singularity," with computers exceeding human understanding and taking real control?

snippet.title: DLD13 - Winner take all (Dambisa Moyo)
snippet.description: When the best performer in a market is able to capture a very large share of the rewards, and the remaining competitors are left with very little, it's called a winner-take-all market. Zambian born economist and thought-provocateuse Dambisa Moyo is presenting her latest book Winner Take All and will speak about the patterns of geo political change, with focus on China's role in the global race for resources. The panel is moderated by Vijay V. Vaitheeswaran, an award-winning senior correspondent for The Economist.

snippet.description: Neurobiologist at the Max Planck Institut Moritz Helmstaedter develops games to explore the brain.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with Rick Smolan
snippet.description: Photographer Rick Smolan gave "big data" a human face through a stunning photojournalism project. Here he talks about the magic of big data in every day life, and the realization that a lot of the power over the floods of informaton lies in the hands of governments and corporations.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with Katharina Borchert
snippet.description: CEO of Spiegel Online Katharina Borchert outlines the benefits of online journalism as well as the challenges that lie ahead, which she sees as an opportunity for journalism.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Delivering Art (Carter Cleveland)
snippet.description: The world of art and e-commerce is merging. In the next five years one of the last industries to resist technological change will take a great leap in the digital sphere. The connective power of the Internet is evolving into a potential bearing device for artists, collectors, and their world in general.

snippet.title: Patterns of your Thoughts (Moran Cerf) | DLD13
snippet.description: Moran Cerf is a neuroscientist who studies how patterns of activity in our brain lead to our behavior, thoughts, emotions and choices. In his talk Moran will show us how some simple activations in the brain can be accessed and used to understand unconscious thoughts that are inaccessible to us, in order to interpreted and predict our future voluntary choices.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Behance - A Platform for Creativity Patterns (Scott Belsky)
snippet.description: Exposing creativity with the help of digital platforms is Scott Belsky's passion. The founder of the online talent pool Behance wants to remove the barriers between talent and opportunity. Behance is the leading online platform to showcase and discover creative work.

snippet.title: Collaborative Creativity (Aaron Koblin, Chris Milk, Johannes Fricke Waldthausen) | DLD13
snippet.description: A conversation about collaborative art with Aaron Koblin and Chris Milk.

snippet.title: What's Next (Amit Shafrir, Pascal Cagni, Abdul Malik Al Jaber, Jeff Pulver, Yossi Vardi) | DLD13
snippet.description: A discussion among the experienced hands about what's next on their personal agenda and the Consumer Internet space.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Communication and Creativity (Kevin Lynch)
snippet.description: A discussion around the various personalities online, from content creator to re-director and how we can better understand the patterns that emerge. What technologies are being built to help better understand and predict patterns in social behavior, communication networks and data streams? How can brands view and understand patterns to reach their customers with the most effective communication possible?

snippet.title: The Third Paradise (Maja Hoffmann, Michelangelo Pistoletto, Hans Ulrich Obrist) | DLD13
snippet.description: Hans Ulrich Obrist talks to Michelangelo Pistoletto about his new book "The third paradise". According to Pistoletto the third paradise is an evolutionary transition in which human intelligence finds ways to coexist with the intelligence of nature.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Wrap Up (Henry Blodget)
Prestige 3.0 (José Neves, Goga Ashkenazi, Sanjiv Singh, Scott Galloway) | DLD13
snippet.description: The importance of prestige in e-commerce is rising. The explosion in prestige sales online will be discussed on the panel as well as seemingly unrelated aspects, such as the impact of Chinese tourists and the aspirations of Amazon. New data points to understand emerging patterns in the fashion sector will be provided.

snippet.title: Patterns that connect (Padmasree Warrior, DJ Patil, Werner Vogels) | DLD13
snippet.description: The modern discipline of data science understands the world around us through patterns of information. Any collection of data, even the obituaries section in a newspaper, has a pattern and can tell us something more than the sum of its individual parts. The expanding processing powers in computer technology allow us to understand complex systems and make simpler connections. What kind of shifts are taking place in science due to the expanding powers of deciphering data.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Emerging Times (José Ramos-Horta, Felix Marquart)
snippet.description: Nobel Peace Prize Laureate José Ramos Horta speaks about the shift from the Western centric approach towards Asia.

snippet.title: Connecting to solve Global Problems differently (Don Tapscott) | DLD13
snippet.description: Don Tapscott will take the stage at this year's DLD and share first findings from the research on how non-state networks may surpass international institutions, like the UN, IMF and World Bank, in their roles as global policy makers. Digital advancement enables these networks to form new patterns of connectivity, which were not possible on this scale ever before.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Burst (Albert-László Barbási)
snippet.description: An introduction into the theories behind Big Data.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Twitter Dress (Francesca Rosella, Ryan Genz)
snippet.description: Fashion in Motion  - Presentation of electronic-powered clothes with LED lights that display real tweets in real time. The clothes of CuteCircuit are rechargeable via USB.

snippet.title: The Israeli Gaming Industry on Stage Party (Leifenberg,Miretzky,Olmert,Sapir,Glassenberg) | DLD13
DLD13 - THE 3D Printing & Manufacturing Revolution (Holman, Weijmarshausen,de Bruijn, Ederer)
snippet.description: In 2013, 3-D printing will increasingly dominate the world's headlines. What does it take to print an Aston Martin for James Bond, food or organs? What is possible and what does it mean for us?

snippet.title: Sleeping Patterns - QS Projects (Till Roenneberg, Esther Dyson) | DLD13
snippet.description: Esther Dyson will elaborate on the reasoning behind investing in sleep, but also pose questions to a man who wrote about clocks. "Not about those you can buy, wear or hang on a wall, but about the clock that ticks in your body" as Prof. Dr. Till Roenneberg writes in his book Internal Time.  Invetsing in  the tech and health sector is one Esther Dyson's ways of impacting society through her invetsments. Der Roenneberg is giving a close-to-life account of why sleep is an important topic for indivduals and investors.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Passage to Clouds (Carson Sweet)
DLD13 - Memories are made of this (Dave Morin)
snippet.description: How does a product evolve which was thought to be mobile first and did not even have a net strategy in the beginning? To what degree is Path competing with his alma mater Facebook today? David Kirkpatrick and Dave Morin will look back on the development of Path and share a definitive view on the mobile shift and search in the mobile world.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Lowline / Underground Gardening (Robyn Shapiro)
DLD13 - How Social Media is changing China and Asia (Kevin Lee, Duncan Clark, Kitty Lun)
snippet.description: Far from being a minor trend, Social Media is having a deep, fast and far-reaching impact on politics, business and culture in China and  across Asia. Join this panel of experts to hear the latest developments and unique Asian innovations.

snippet.title: DLD13 -  Hollywood meets Silicon Valley - Part II (Guy Oseary)
snippet.description: There is still a disconnect between Hollywood and Silicon Valley. Their culture and DNA have not yet been synched. The fund Ashton Kutcher and Guy Oseary started two years ago, called A-Grade, s now the most proactive and successful tech investment fund from Hollywood. One example of reaping the benefits from this kind of collaboration is Spotify which has gone from a hundred thousand paying subscribers to 5million paying subscribers. Who's going to be next?

snippet.title: DLD13 - Game Based Brain Reconstruction (Moritz Helmstädter)
snippet.description: Moritz Helmstädter, scientist at the Max Planck Institute and an expert in neurobiology, focuses on brain mapping with the help of electronic microscopic data in a playful way: he developed the computer game "Brain Flight" that reconstructs the brains of mice in 3D with the assistance of crowdsourcing techniques.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Future of Screens II (Stefan Schulz)
snippet.description: Smart TV offers new possibilities for users to actively participate in the TV program and to be involved in real-time. They can participate in live TV shows via "dial-in" or watch movies "on demand" at their preferred time. The future of TV is interactive and social. The panel takes a look into the future of television and explains the technical features of modern TV and what lays beyond.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Future of Screens (Lutz Schüler, Lisa Donovan, Samir Arora, Christian Wegner)
snippet.description: Smart TV offers new possibilities for users to actively participate in the TV program and to be involved in real-time. They can participate in live TV shows via "dial-in" or watch movies "on demand" at their preferred time. The future of TV is interactive and social. The panel takes a look into the future of television and explains the technical features of modern TV and what lays beyond.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with Mallika Chopra
snippet.description: Founder of intent.com Mallika Chopra shares her ideas on how networks and communities can change the world in small and big ways.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Finance your Idea (Sunil Madhu, Sebastian Siemiatkovski, Alexa von Tobel)
snippet.description: Both sides of financing are leveraging the resources of the crowd and big data. This panel explores and discusses a range of new opportunities from fund seekers who improve decision making to financers tapping into new ways of credit evaluation.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Direct Access (Gary Swart, Oleg Tscheltzoff, Danae Ringelmann, David Liu)
snippet.description: The most impactful technological advancements are not in the once-dreamed-about realm of jetpacks and flying cars — they are the ones that enable on-demand access to critical resources, without the friction of intermediation. On this panel, three businesses that are emblematic of this disruptive shift towards direct access will discuss how the next generation of technology is changing the way businesses compete.

snippet.title: DLD13 -  Creativity & Entrepreneurship: Europe vs. US (Hidary, Arvai, Shank, Varsavsky)
snippet.description: What does it take to start a business in our times? Does it matter whether your company is based in Europe or in Silicon Valley? Are the threats and opportunities the same? What it takes to become an entrepreneur varies greatly from country to country. Jack D. Hidary, entrepreneur and CEO of the Hidary Foundation, and Martin Varsavsky who founded his company FON in Europe are on stage to dismantle patterns in the American and European way of entrepreneurship.

snippet.title: Aenne Burda Award (Zaha Hadid) | DLD13
snippet.description:
And the winner of this year's Aenne Burda Award is Zaha Hadid!
Interview by Hans Ulrich Obrist.

snippet.title: Music (Ganes Parores & Neores) | DLD13
snippet.description: Music Act at DLD13.

snippet.title: Creative Ways to Sell (Oskar Hartmann, Frederic Court, Hjalmar Winbladh, S.Afra, S.Winners) | DLD13
snippet.description: There is an increasing blending of the former online/offline separation and new models are evolving with win-win situations both for online and stationary players. In this panel, we will explore what makes these models successful and whether this will result in a more fundamental change of the ecommerce space.

snippet.title: Pattern Shift: Warming World, Rising Risks (J.Meier, E.Rauch, O.R.Grimsson, D.Kenny) | DLD13
snippet.description: Icelandic innovation is taking place on a large scale: a new shipping route is developed due to melting glaciers. Changing weather patterns require us to "manage the unavoidable" and "avoid the unmanageable". While weather might be unpredictable, climate changes are not. Are we prepared for these changing patterns in our environment, and where could they lead?

snippet.title: DLD13 - Data and Risk (Max Levchin)
snippet.description: Max Levchin is presenting his project "HVF". HVF searches relentlessly for opportunities that create value by leveraging data. This takes form of seed and early stage investing, rapid prototyping of internally-generated ideas, getting together with the brightest minds in the many industries that will benefit form the data explosion, looking for interesting data sets and sources, and just geeking out on data.

snippet.title: A Drop in the Amazon (Ruchi Sanghvi, Werner Vogels) | DLD13
snippet.description: Our behavioral patterns in storing and accessing our information is reaching new levels with cloud based devices like Dropbox and providers like Amazon. The simplicity of customer driven product design comes together with complex operating systems. A look behind the scenes.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Searching the Universe (Arkady Volozh)
snippet.description: Can algorithms tell what physical world we are living in?

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with Lisa Donovan
snippet.description: Co-founder of Maker Studios and YouTube personality Lisa Donovan talks about developments in the online business of marketing and content creation.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with Kitty Lun
snippet.description: Kitty Lun is a leading creator in China's LOWE agency. She shares her insights on advertising in the time of digital transformation in a booming market.

snippet.title: Next Generation Search (Wolf Garbe, Albert Wenger) | DLD13
snippet.description: Decentralization is the foundation of the internet. It fostered diversity and freedom of information. So why copy the entire internet to one system? Does this sound strange to you? This is what search engines do today. That's why we have to talk about what's next in search and how we can overcome prohibitively expensive infrastructure that infringes on competition and innovation.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with Kevin Lee
snippet.description: Understanding China's coming generations is the quest of China Youthology - Kevin Lee is the think tank's CEO and shares his insights on the booming nation.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with Erik Wikström
snippet.description: CEO of Magine Erik Wikström shares his ideas about the future of television.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with Duncan Clark
snippet.description: Investment advisor and chairman of BDA Duncan Clark talks about his experience from working in China for more than 10 years.

snippet.title: Interview with David Kenny (CEO at The Weather Channel) | DLD13
snippet.description: The Weather Channel's CEO David Kenny talks about climate change and how we can use data to understand and cope with increasingly extreme weather conditions.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with Aaron Koblin
snippet.description: Digital artist Aaron Koblin on why he's a techno-optimist.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Hacking is the new Power (Keren Elazari)
snippet.description: The Israeli cyber security expert with three years of training in cybernetics explains how hacking can be a new form of power in he 21st Century. She showcases how taking things apart is a source for innovation. Keren Elazari is inspired by the forms of political empowerment and social interaction which the modern hacking culture is supporting.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with Stefania Druga
snippet.description: Stefania believes in disrupting the education sector. She is a former Singularity fellow and active with HacKIDemia (www.hackidemia.com) where she introduces kids to the culture of hacking.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with René Schuster
snippet.description: Telefonica CEO Renè Schuster shares his insights on how mobile devices will shape our every day lives.

snippet.title: Interview with Moran Cerf | DLD13
snippet.description: Neuroscientist and visionary Moran Cerf talks about how technology can help us to understand our brains.

snippet.title: Interview with Joe Gebbia (Co-founder of AirBnB) | DLD13
snippet.description: AirBnB co-founder Joe Gebbia talks about how the sharing economy is akin to the  infrastructure of Ancient Rome and why design still informs all of his doing.

snippet.title: DLD13 - What's holding back the Data Revolution (DJ Patil)
snippet.description: The modern discipline of data science understands the world around us through patterns of information. Dj Patil himself coined the term data scientist, which according to him, is the sexiest job of the 21st Century. A data scientist to him is like an explorer, making discoveries in the exotic mountains of data and floods of digital information. He will take us on a journey to the current "hot spots" of the data revolution.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Extreme Bionics 8Hugh Herr, Reinhold Messner)
snippet.description: Half the world's population currently suffers from some form of physical or neurological disability. But what if, through the invention and deployment of novel technologies, human disability could be eradicated? Extreme Bionics is a research agenda to eliminate disability in this century,  extending human physicality, cognition and creativity beyond what nature intended.

snippet.title: DLD13 - DLD Arts Book Launch (Johannes Fricke Waldthausen, Chris Rehberger)
DLD13 - Future of mobile payment IV (René Schuster, Markus Braun, David Marcus)
snippet.description: The future of money is digital. Instead of carrying credit cards or cash around we will more and more use our smartphone as a safe and convenient way to make daily payments. An industry discussion on the road forward and roadblocks.

snippet.title: Cyberwarfare, Crime and Security (Eugene Kaspersky, Mikko Hypponen, Dan Dubno) | DLD13
snippet.description: This session will look at cyber crime and security from several perspectives and will challenge perceptions surrounding the increasing threat of cyber attacks on governments and society.

snippet.title: A Visionairs Keynote (Eugene Kaspersky) | DLD13
snippet.description: The threat of cyber warfare has become reality. Governments are waking up to the dangers of cybercrime and are looking for solutions. But who are the criminals and who are the hackers with good intentions?

snippet.title: Introduction (Dan Dubno, Blowing Things Up) | DLD13
Learning about Creative Leadership - A Friendship Tale (Joe Gebbia, AirBnB & John Maeda) | DLD13
snippet.description: A conversation between John Maeda of the Rhode Island School of Design and Joe Gebbia of AirBnB exploring the intersection of design, business, and education. Companies like Airbnb, Square, and Apple are demonstrating the benefit of nurturing creativity within their organizations and along they way they are carrying design from the studio into the boardroom.  Together Joe and his former teacher John will talk about the changing face of business and explain why design will play a crucial role in shaping the future.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with Johannes Meier
snippet.description: CEO of the European Climate Foundation Johannes Meier talks about the relevance of economic subsidies and the role of militaries in relation to global climate change.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with Gabriele Oettingen
snippet.description: Experimental psychologist Gabriele Oettingen demystifies the "positive thinking" trap.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Future of mobile payment I (David Marcus)
snippet.description: As mobile payment has become reality David Marcus of Paypal and ACCEL's Joe Schoendorf embark on a visionary discussion on the connection between mobile payment and user data. They bring forward products that mix geolocation data and mobile payment that we consumers wish to have today rather than tomorrow.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Future of mobile payment III (Markus Braun)
snippet.description: Wirecard's Markus Braun will bring up facts and figures about mobile payment and discuss the latest developments of in-app payment with Roman Friedrich of Booz & Co.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Future of mobile payment II (René Schuster)
snippet.description: From network provider to mobile payment provider. A discussion on how Telefonica is well on its way to become a financial institution and what lays ahead of us.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Industry Outlook (Henrique de Castro)
DLD13 - Digital Marketing (Lang, Read, Hospital, Heinemann, Rubenstein)
snippet.description: The panel is dealing with new trends and upcoming problems in online advertising. Key topics are: Data Driven Display Advertising, Mobile Monetization, Social Media Advertising, Multi Channel Advertising and Brandvertising.

snippet.title: Giants vs. Consumers (Terence Kawaja, Founder and CEO at LUMA Partners) | DLD13
snippet.description: A keynote about the battle among internet giants for the digital consumer.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Biosynthetic Architecture (Mitchell Joachim)
snippet.description: Terreform ONE [Open Network Ecology] is the official non-profit design group that promotes green design in cities. Through the use of biosynthetic materials architecture connects to bioscience. Will this overthrow existing patterns in city architecture and design?

snippet.title: DIY Science Lab (Ellen Jorgensen & Oliver Medvedik, GenSpace) | DLD13
snippet.description: Genetic code is what GenSpace brings to the masses with simple tools at ever decreasing cost. As a non-profit organization they are promoting citizen science and access to biotechnology which you can experience right at DLD where they will showcase what it takes to decode your genetic code.

snippet.title: 21st Century Statecraft (Alec Ross, Johns Hopkins University & Nick Bilton) | DLD13
snippet.description: The emergence of new information and communication technologies catalyzes change in national politics and international relations. Connectivity changes the way citizens behave and lays the foundation for novel ways to do politics, from winning elections with the help of data science to new communication and information tools for foreign politics.

snippet.title: DLD13 - There will be Light (Jacques-Philippe Piverger, Jill van den Brule)
snippet.description: This ASHOKA-panel shines a light on the dangerous implications of energy poverty around the world: Luci Lamp is an inflatable, water resistant, bright LED solar lantern. It's maintenance-free, recharges in the sun and is durable and reliable in extreme conditions. The Buy One Give One model will help to bring light to parts of the world where electricity is a daily challenge.

snippet.title: Coding the Future (Zachary Sims, Founder of Codecademy & Rohan Silva) | DLD13
snippet.description: Bringing programming to the masses to decode the present and code the future. 22 year old Zach Sims, founder of Codecademy, talks about his education platform. Codecademy is an online interactive platform that offers free coding classes in programming languages like Python, JavaScript, and Ruby, as well as markup languages including HTML and CSS.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with Mitchell Joachim
snippet.description: Mitchell Joachim from Terreform One - the ecological and architectural design group from Brooklyn, NY - talks about growing chairs and why not all clever minds should end up on Wall Street.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with Michal Juda
snippet.description: Michal Juda is co-founder of Showroom - a Polish designer start-up going global.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Baba's Guide to Evolution (Baba Brinkman, Jamie Simmonds)
snippet.description: The Rap Guide to Evolution is a one-man hip-hop show, entertaining and accessible, with lyrics that have been scientifically fact-checked for accuracy. It covers topics as diverse as evolutionary psychology, the Canterbury Tales, democracy, and civil disobedience.

snippet.title: Patterns of Connectivity (John Hering, Klaus Hommels, René Obermann, Diane Brady) | DLD13
snippet.description: A discussion on investing, partnerships and innovation in a connected environment and patterns that emerge on a micro and macro level.

snippet.title: DLD13 - The Big Push (Claudia Gonzalez)
snippet.description: Everyone can play a role to make the world a better place. That's what the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria's Big Push campaign is all about. It has brought together the digital media community and art world to end these diseases of once and for all.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Ben's Blog (Ben Horowitz)
snippet.description: Ben Horowitz, venture capitalist and digital entrepreneur, is talking with the founders of Rap Genius about the evolution of startups. The potential of Rap Genius is likely to go beyond the love for rhythm and rhyme. Only a handful of people know that the big missing feature from the first web browser was the ability to annotate any page on the Internet with commentary and additional information. Rap Genius provides the technological foundations to finally bring in this missing feature. Annotating the web is like getting a glimpse of the future in the patterns of the web.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Annotate the World (Mahbod Moghadam, Ilan Zechory, Tom Lehman)
snippet.description: Ben Horowitz, venture capitalist and digital entrepreneur, is talking with the founders of Rap Genius about the evolution of startups. The potential of Rap Genius is likely to go beyond the love for rhythm and rhyme. Only a handful of people know that the big missing feature from the first web browser was the ability to annotate any page on the Internet with commentary and additional information. Rap Genius provides the technological foundations to finally bring in this missing feature. Annotating the web is like getting a glimpse of the future in the patterns of the web.

snippet.title: DLD13 - Human Face of Big Data (Rick Smolan)
snippet.description: The photographer Rick Smolan unveils what we mean with big data and allows us to visualize it with mindblowing photographs. Big data is more than the information that fits on a personal computer, it is the tools that show the patterns within it. It is the planet's digital nervous system, and we interact with it as just another human type of sensor.

snippet.title: Campus Lecture by Peter Thiel | DLD13
snippet.description: Peter Thiel from Founders Fund talks to students at LMU in Munich about the "Last Mover Advantage".

snippet.title: DLD13 - Interview with Andrew Keen & Jon Miller
DLD Arts Project (Aaron Koblin, Google & Chris Milk) | DLD13
snippet.description: Aaron Koblin and Chris Milk will take us into an exquisite forest of data and animations.  They let users create short animations that build off one another as they explore a specific theme. The result is a collection of branching narratives collectively built on Google Chrome's HTML5 and JavaScript support, as well as Google App Engine and Google Cloud Storage. This collaborative art project is open for all DLD guests to join and the artwork is presented on Tuesday before the closing keynote takes place.

snippet.title: DLD13 - The Power of Lifestyle Changes, Social Networks and Love (Dean Ornish)
snippet.description: Identifying obstacles in lifestyle-patterns and overcoming them is a route to success. Not only if we want to pursue desired futures but also in demonstrating that comprehensive lifestyle changes may slow, stop, or even reverse diseases such as prostate cancer or heart disease as Dean Ornish proved in his research. He will be in conversation with Gabriele Oettingen who adds to the idea of changing our behavioral patterns by becoming more aware of the perils in positive thinking. She will present the results of 15 years of research on this topic.

snippet.title: Future Of Authority (K.Borchert, A.Sulzberger Jr., J.Jarvis, M.Nisenholtz, I.Osborne) | DLD13
snippet.description: A long time ago journalists were an authority and readers relied on them to inform them about events they didn't witness or experienced themselves. Today, tens of thousands of people use Twitter and Facebook to give their own accounts of events such as uprisings or other happenings around the globe. How does this development affect the creed of journalism? What does it mean for governments and what does it mean for business leaders? As mass communication technology becomes available to huge numbers of citizens, where does authority lie today and how does it reshape the role of journalists?

DLD10 - Interview with Norman Foster
snippet.description:
Norman Foster is one of the most important architects practising in the world today. His practice, Foster + Partners, is based in London but has project offices worldwide. Since its foundation in 1967, the practice has pioneered a sustainable approach to architecture and ecology through a strikingly wide range of projects, from urban masterplans, airports, civic and cultural buildings, offices and workplaces to private houses and product design.

Foster has completed projects as diverse as the Reichstag, Berlin's new Parliament, Chek Lap Kok International Airport in Hong Kong and the Great Court at the British Museum in London. Recent work includes the Hearst Tower New York, Millau Viaduct in France and Beijing Airport. Norman Foster was appointed to the Order of Merit by the Queen in 1997. In 1999 he was honoured with a life peerage, taking the title Lord Foster of Thames Bank and won the Pritzker Architecture Prize the same year.

snippet.title: DLD Interview with Tan Le
snippet.description: Ms Tan Le is Founder and CEO of Emotive Life Sciences, a bioinformatics comany that is using electroencephalography to identify biomarkers in the brain for mental and other neurological conditions. Her main goal is to create a cloud which can hold a huge amount of information about the brain to detect very early biomarkers that realte to mental diseases. Her second goal is to develop and establish an easy way in collecting data with her affordable and wireless EGG headset which she has invented.

snippet.title: DLD Interview with Brij Kothari
snippet.description: Mr Brij Kothari is the Founder of Planet Read. The innovation of this company is called "same language subtitling". The subtitling of lyrics for Bollywood film songs on mainstream Television is a way of giving reading preactice to over 300 million people who can not read. The integration of this into the everyday entertainment makes reading inescapable. Mr Brij Kothari wants to extend this project to parts of Asia and Africa.

snippet.title: Interview with Peter Diamandis (Chairman and CEO at X-Prize Foundation) | DLD12
snippet.description:
Dr. Peter Diamandis is an American engineer, physician, entrepreneur, book author and above all an optimist. 
His latest book "Abundance - The Future is Better Than You Think" is an antidote to today's dark pessimism: It argues that new technologies and other forces will make the coming years better, not worse, as we so often worry. 
He is also the Chairman and CEO of the X PRIZE Foundation, which leads the world in designing and launching large incentive prizes to drive radical breakthroughs for the benefit of humanity. One of their latest projects is the Qualcomm Tricorder X PRIZE which is a $10 million competition for building a mobile device to diagnose and monitor healthcare conditions. 
As Peter says: "The more the people and the planet become interconnected, the better we are. I am an optimist and evidence shows that there is a good reason for that."

snippet.title: DLD Moscow 2012- Interview with Eric Schuldenfrei
snippet.description:
„In the next 20 years, China will add 350 million people to cities. That's basically the population of the U.S.," says Eric Schuldenfrei. At DLD Moscow, the architect shared some of his first-hand experiences from building China from scratch. Fighting against the mere replication of the same concrete blocks over and over again - a routine that is especially dominant in the second-tier cities in the Chinese hinterland, unknown places that yet house 20 million people -- he opts for a communicative alternative and rethinks how technology can be implemented.

Arguing against the seperation of functionalities, he advocates to reconsider the ancient idea of a city that is intermixed instead. That includes to put he human being in the centre again: „You build the community first and then see what type of infrastructure supports that."

DLDwomen 12 - Interview with Kah Walla
snippet.description:
"How does technology enable us to get access to water? How does it enable us to get access to health care? How do we fast-track education using technology?" asks Kah Walla, one of Cameroon's political leaders and entrepreneurs, who manages to inspire an entire generation. In the case of her country, 50% of the people don't have access to electricity and clean water.
 
For her continent, she says in an interview with Lukas Kubina at DLDwomen 2012, technology is seen as a tool to help close the development gap. "For us Africans we're using it to make a gigantic leap," she says. It gives a voice to people who traditionally are not part of the power structure, like women and young people. In Africa, where there are still a number of totalitarian governments, the Internet is becoming an alternative source of information for people.
 
Although Internet penetration is still very low in most of sub-Saharan Africa, 10% or less, the people who are on the Internet are innovators. "They are thought leaders," Walla says. With their spirit of creativity, she argues, "just putting the technology in the hands of people is going to enable us to really reveal extraordinary things."
 
First, basic infrastructure needs to be provided, says Walla. She means access to the Internet, broadband cables, and computers for everyone. This is the final ignition for the African leap.

snippet.title: Interview with Ida Tin (CEO and Co-Founder of BioWink) | DLDwomen 12
DLDwomen 12 - Interview with Gabi Zedlmayer
snippet.description:
"It's a fantastic time for women," says Gabi Zedlmayer, Vice President of HP's Office of Global Social Innovation at the DLDwomen conference 2012. "New rules will apply," she adds. Zedlmayer is one of the rare female role models in tech who not only inspire others but also take action. She takes lab and business innovations and applies them to social causes.
 
As one of the founding friends of DLD, we've always followed her work to tackle critical social issues in education and health through strategic collaborations with non-profits and social entrepreneurs to serve developing communities around the world. She really deserves all imaginable attention for this outstanding personal effort.
 
One project she highlights in this interview with Lukas Kubina, HP's Early Infant Diagnosis program, started 18 months ago. Alongside the Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI) in Africa, Zedlmayer improved the speed of HIV diagnosis for infants in Kenya. "When children are born, and their blood gets analyzed for HIV, often the test results get back after four months," she says. "That's about three months too late." She cut down that time to 20 days for 65,000 babies in one year. This project demonstrates that technology has the potential to make a difference and save lives by getting accurate, timely information in the hands of the people who need it.
 
She puts 'heart work' into her projects. That's what makes her impact grow throughout the world. "We're taking this methodology, this reference case, to many other countries that really need the same kind of application," she says. In countries like Uganda, Tanzania and South Africa the Health Ministry is already replicating what Zedlmayer started in Kenya.
 
That's called having a true impact.

For her dedication in maximizing results from the philanthropic efforts of HP, Gabi Zedlmayer received the DLDwomen Impact Award 2012.

snippet.title: DLD Moscow 2012 - Interview with Ekatarina Gaika
Interview with Shamim Sarif (Enlightenment Productions) | DLD12
snippet.description:
The rare talent to envision stories in pictures turned Shamim Sarif into an equally successful novelist, screenwriter and film director. That's because her descriptive power of a storyteller meets a screenwriter's mastery of dialogue. She's used to winning awards and still finds the urge to challenge societal perceptions.

"My head is in the clouds with the story," she said in this interview with Lukas Kubina.

A hypnotic combination of love and tragic loss at the pace of a thriller -- Despite the Falling Snow is supposed to take your breath away. Sarif's second book moves between present day Boston and 1950s snowbound streets of post-Stalinist Moscow. The author's delicate writing makes this novel outstanding, once again. Its film production is on the way, promising artistry filled with suspense.

snippet.title: Interview with Juliana Rotich (Executive Director at Ushahidi) | DLD12
snippet.description:
Refering to herself as "African geek girl", Juliana Rotich is an evangelist for African ICT and how it impacts the lives of many people across the continent. She has just moved back to Nairobi and her tireless work towards getting Africa out of the so called 'Digital Divide' cannot not be stopped by power outages or angry neighbours like Sudan or Somalia.

The role and success of mobile based technologies in the developing world cannot be underestimated. As much these technologies have positively impacted the lives of many, Juliana is sure that mobile technology will exponentially develop in Africa. In the second part of the interview, she shares some leap-frogging innovation from Africa.

snippet.title: Interview with Juliana Rotich (Executive Director at Ushahidi) | DLD12
snippet.description:
Refering to herself as "African geek girl", Juliana Rotich is an evangelist for African ICT and how it impacts the lives of many people across the continent. She has just moved back to Nairobi and her tireless work towards getting Africa out of the so called 'Digital Divide' cannot not be stopped by power outages or angry neighbours like Sudan or Somalia.

Like many Kenyans in diaspora, she found herself drawn into the crisis when violence hit Kenya after the national elections in December 2008. Being pro-active she collaborated with the online community and helped in founding Ushahidi.

Ushahidi is a web based reporting system that utilises crowdsourced data to formulate visual map information of a crisis on a real-time basis. In the Kenyan scenario it was used to map out incidents of violence and this information has played a crucial role in the continuing justice and reconciliation process in Kenya. Ushahidi then grew to be an open source incident reporting platform that has been successfully deployed in various situations such as Haiti earthquake, the Palestine conflict crisis, heavy snow crisis in Washington or commodity prices in Afghanistan. 

The role and success of mobile based technologies in the developing world cannot be underestimated. As much these technologies have positively impacted the lives of many, Juliana is sure that mobile technology will exponentially develop in Africa. 

At DLD12, she shared the status quo of her undertakings and spotlights some leap-frogging innovators from Africa.
