snippet.title: DLD Moscow - Interview with Sasha Galitsky
snippet.description: Well known as "Sasha", his nickname dates back to his time in the Soviet space industry where he did critical development in the Russian Star Wars Response. Today, Alexander Galitsky is one of the most influential persons in the Russian tech industry. A tech pioneer, serial entrepreneur, venture capitalist, and Skokolvo board member, you might find him in the Kremlin or hanging out at Eric Schmidt's office at Google headquarters in Silicon Valley on any given day. At DLD Moscow he shares snippets of his biography and explains some specific rules to  Europe's largest tech market.

snippet.title: Interview with Marco Boerries (Founder and CEO at NumberFour AG) | DLD12
snippet.description:
Marco Börries has been in the digital hall of fame for more than 25 years. "Making ideas work and turning them into reality," he explains his biggest talent. The mastermind behind OpenOffice.org has just been part of the delegation, which met German chancellor Angela Merkel for the "Internetgipfel" (english: Internet Summit) on June 4, 2012. 

Discussing particular requirements and factors for a booming digital sector, the dialogue between government officials and representatives of the Internet economy aims to improve the framework for the German start-up scene. 

In this interview, the DLD all time alumni is touching the notion of privacy and the increasing involvement of governments. He advocates not to destroy the most democratising vehicle in the world (Internet) by balkanizing it into fragments.

snippet.title: DLD Moscow - Interview with Lapo Elkann
snippet.description:
"Fashion fades but style is eternal." Thus the timeless Yves Saint Laurent differentiated between two terms that are still getting confused frequently. In the light of Lapo Elkann's appearance, it evidently passes on and is an Italian trait, too. "I am not someone who likes fashion," he says cheekily, "I follow style."

With his brisk inclination towards the wild side and his seemingly unintentional elegance, the rakish grandson of Gianni Agnelli is the perfect (re)incarnation of the Italian playboy. Beyond his sartorial flair, Lapo is a brilliant marketeer and entrepreneur.

In this interview, he shares some of his abundant ideas on design, creativity, propositions and real luxury. "One needs to be hungry and daring," he says in reference to Steve Jobs's famous credo.* "From a one €uro Bic lighter to a Ferrari of six million €uros, it's not a matter of money, it is about giving options: a rich person and a poor person; they want cool shit, they want fun stuff!"

*One needs to be foolish and hungry

snippet.title: Interview with Kevin Slavin (Co-Founder of Area/Code) | DLD12
snippet.description: Mighty Kevin Slavin talks about the role of cities for the new generation of start-ups. New York City and Berlin - both cities that only a few years ago weren't considered as great soil for tech start ups - have reached serious gravity and are growing to be centres of innovation. He argues that's because new business models are more about the interaction of people in the real world and using technology to facilitate that. 'There's a reason why location based services are developping in cities filled with people.'

snippet.title: Interview with Caroline Drucker (Product Manager at SoundCloud) | DLD12
snippet.description: Caroline Drucker just got back from the road to join DLD12. Having departed from a scene of early adopters in electronic music, Berlin based Soundcloud became the social platform for audio sharing - ranging from Snoop Dogs Tecno Euro Mixx (http://soundcloud.com/snoopdogg/01-tekno-euro-mixx) to the sound of London's Southbank Skate Park (http://soundcloud.com/binauraldiaries/southbank-skate-park-london). In this interview, she talks about her trip to the Valley and deep integration.

snippet.title: Interview with Dimitar Sasselov (Harvard University) | DLD12
snippet.description: Dimitar Sasselov is a Professor of Astronomy at Harvard University and founder of the Harvard Origins of Life Initiative. In this DLD12 interview, the Bulgarian scientist presents his groundbreaking book `Life On Super-Earths' and sheds light on the key role of interdisciplinarity. Explaining the magic of DLD, he shares the experiences he had collected at the 'Go To Space' breakfast with George Whitesides (CEO, Virgin Galactic), Eric Anderson (CEO, Space Adventures), and Peter Diamandis, introduced by Esther Dyson. 'Something which brings our dreams of going to space to reality.'

snippet.title: Interview with Slava Rubin (Co-Founder and CEO at Indie Gogo) | DLD12
snippet.description: Slava Rubin is CEO and co-founder of IndieGoGo which provides anyone with opportunity to fund creative, entrepreneurial, or cause campaigns. The service has been used for over 50,000 campaigns and distributed millions of dollars globally.  In 2011, IndieGoGo was named one of the partner companies for Startup America - President Obama's initiative to stimulate entrepreneurship in America. At #DLD12, Slava talks about the concept, its track record and mentions that crowdfunding is at least as old as the Statue of Liberty.

snippet.title: FOCUS Nightcap Davos | DLD12
Interview with Ellen Jorgensen (Executive Director at Genspace) | DLD12
snippet.description:
Remember when science was fun? Ellen Jorgensen wants to bring back this  euphoria last seen in the Space Race. With the Genspace NYC, the Do-It-Yourself Biotech Lab in Brooklyn, she is pioneering in Citizen Science beyond commercial restrictions. Learn more about this cutting-edge project in this DLD12 interview. 

For further information check out her DLD12 talk at http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LXOM5tVjxtc and visit: http://genspace.org/

snippet.title: Interview with Rodrigo Baggio (Center for Digital Inclusion, CDI) | DLD12
snippet.description:
Rodrigo Baggio spearheads the CDI - Committee for Democracy in Information Technology. By installing self managed community centres, it uses technology to develop low income communities. In this interview at DLD12, he shows how it helped the indigineous Anshanikas in the Brazilian Amazonas to defend their rainforest. Furthermore, he advocates social inclusion in the face of Brazi's economic boom.

At DLD12 he was part of the social entrepreneur session which you find here: http://bit.ly/yliLAU // Rodrigo Baggio is an Ashoka Fellow. Learn more about it here: http://bit.ly/hvGtmA

snippet.title: Interview with Raul Krauthausen (wheelmap.org) | DLD12
snippet.description:
Raul Krauthausen is a notorious trailblazer. The social entrepreneur explains how his project wheelmap.org enables millions and what role crowdsourcing plays. Basically, the platform allows it's users to geotag information about the level of accessibilty of POIs. Thus, it makes possible a feedback loop on city infrastructure, applies pressure on certain localities and simply is a source of information about whether or not a spot is wheelchair accessible or not.

At DLD11 he was a panellist on the "Responsive Cities" session (http://bit.ly/xXk5xT).

snippet.title: The DLD New York Breakfast Club - Esther Dyson
snippet.description:
Esther Dyson is invariably ahead of time. She has both the brains and instincts to make this a certainty. When she is not looking at potential investments or is fighting for government transparency, she had been training to be a cosmonaut. Her early investment in Personal Genome Service 23andMe was a great hint. Looking at her steadily reinforced angel investments in healthcare, the prediction of the next big thing comes easy.
 
As technology advances, it is increasingly easy to collect personal health and fitness data to help us combat our own vices such as laziness, alcohol or bad food. She firmly believes that user generated data and personal devices like Jawbone can make us healthier. The underlying motivation is not only obsession for personal health but also very social. Comparing the completed kilometres on a bycycle for instance, you can compete with your social network and health is getting gamificated.

snippet.title: DLD Breakfast Club NYC - Arthur O. Sulzberger Jr. (New York Times)
snippet.description:
The New York Times adopted early to what was later labelled the ‚digital revolution.' In a time when many traditional media companies were still self-confidently and complacently looking at the Internet as a contemporary phenomenon,  the NYT launched it's first online platform -- ‚The Times on the Web' - in January 1996. 

At the General Assembly in NYC, Arthur joined us for the DLD 'morning party'. Meet him and learn more about new significant changes like a digital subscription model for the NYT in the interview below.

snippet.title: DLD Breakfast Club NYC - Daniel Kahneman
snippet.description:
Daniel Kahneman is a psychologist who was awarded the 2002 Nobel Prize in Economics. He turned psychology into a quantitative science and thus achieved a new understanding of economics. By analyzing how we deal with dollars and cents, he broke down our mental processes to exact measurement and calculation. His ongoing work on judgement, decision-making, and behavioral economics just put him on the Bloomberg ‚50 Most Influential People in Global Finance' list.
 
Dismantling the homo oeconomicus and spotlighting human irrationality are Kahneman's thing. In his recently published book ‚Thinking, Fast and Slow' a large part is dedicated to stories illustrating the illusions by which the ‚rational' decision-maker is fooled. His stories uncover how far our actual behavior differs from the behavior of the mythical "rational actor" who obeys the rules of classical economics.
 
At the General Assembly in NYC, the former DLD speaker joined us for the DLD 'morning party'. Meet him and learn more about his dual concept of fast and slow thinking as well as how stereotypes are based in our representation of the world in the interview below.

snippet.title: DLD Tel Aviv Interview 2011 - Idit Harel Caperton
snippet.description:
As the founder and president of WorldWideWorkshop, Idit Harel Caperton is developing social learning networks to cultivate innovation and creativity among youth. Computer technology for her is the perfect tool to present learning environments to everyone, in particular to minorities all over the world. She in particular tries to reach kids and their parents, wherever they are based, to enable them to believe in their ideas and to pursue those ideas until they may become a prototype and in the end a product. 

"It is a human right", Idit Harel at DLD Tel Aviv argues, "to be informed not only as a consumer, but also as a creator and pusher of one`s ideas". So as one of the programs of her organisation, she installed the Globaloria Game Design Competitions, a social learning network, teaching students to invent educational webgames. "To be digital citizens in democratic societies, we must be aware, that our most important commodity is education", she summarizes her mission. Meet Idit Harel in the video below to also discuss, why social media should be better used for social purposes.

snippet.title: DLD Tel Aviv 2011 - Interview with Michal Levy
snippet.description:
As a child, Michal Levy used to express her emotions equally in painting, dancing and music. Twenty years later, as she told at DLD Tel Aviv, she discovered, that her synesthetic intelligence was much more than a talent, it was her destiny. At the Jerusalem Bezalel Academy of Arts and Design, she studied visual communication and experienced, that digital technology could become her vehicle in connecting music and visuals. So, as her thesis project, she produced her first music-animated short film "Giant Steps", which became a huge success, being viewed by more than one million people online and being presented in galleries, magazines and on festivals around the world.
 
Being a saxophone player herself, Levy translated "Giant Steps" from 1959, the groundbreaking Album of American Jazz-Saxophonist John Coltrane, into congenial visual architecture. Soon "One" followed as her second music-animation, again documenting, what Michal claims to be her artistic challenge: "I want to understand, how music looks and to communicate to as many people as possible what I see, when I hear". Meet Michal Levy in the video below to learn more about the colors of music.

snippet.title: DLD Tel Aviv 2011 - Interview with Dov Ganchrow
snippet.description: The man, who issues this statement, together with his partner Ami Drach back in 1996 started their Dov Ganchrow & Ami Drach-Design Studio-Partnership in Tel Aviv. Humor, American born Ganchrow claims to be the red line through their wide range of projects covering medical product design as well as museum exhibitions, furniture and lightning. To design in our postindustrial society, he explains at DLD Tel Aviv, means, to "communicate through objects". The special qualities of Israeli design Ganchrow describes as being conceptual, coming from words and thoughts more than from materials and form. "It is about, what lies behind the form", he claims. "We are forming ideas, and ideas can take on many forms". To experience, why Ganchrow thinks Israeli design to be in particular up to date, go to the video below.

snippet.title: DLD Breakfast Club NYC - Felix Petersen (AMEN)
snippet.description:
As experienced entrepreneur (Plazes, Amen) as well as active investor and advisor to companies like Soundcloud and Unlike, Felix Petersen is right at the epicenter of the über-hyped Berlin start-up culture. With his latest venture Amen, he has done nothing else but taking the social to biblical terms. Based on the antipodes 'Amen' and 'Hell No', he has gone berserk and basically invented the 'Unlike' button. Whether it is movie-buffs in a basement in Minnesota, foodies in San Franciso or Berlin hippsters cataloguing the nightlife, these two extremes guarantee that only the extraordinary things are featured; the best and worst of everything.

At the General Assembly in NYC, Felix came out and joined us for the DLD 'morning party'. Meet him and find out more about the business model behind Amen as well as if it's innate of a typical Berlin DNA in the interview below.

snippet.title: DLD Tel Aviv 2011 - Interview with Davor Magdic
snippet.description: He started his professional career as an engineer in Belgrade, then five years ago, Serbian born Davor Magdic went to Santa Barbara in California to become a software engineer. Since 2008 he is president of Visikord, specializing in designing dance-reactive visuals. Visikord he describes as a computer software for playing visual music with the dancer`s body: "With my visuals I want to capture this unique feeling, how a person feels the music of another person", he tells at the DLD Tel Aviv Summit. Meanwhile DJs around the globe are working with Davor and many people enjoy Visikord as an ultimate party accessory. To learn more about this new software, go the video below.

snippet.title: DLD Tel Aviv 2011 - Interview with Tal Shoham
snippet.description:
In the Event-Business Tal Shoham during the last years has gained a lot of global experience. After studying Law and Eastern Asia Studies at Tel Aviv University, Mandarin-Chinese speaking Tal Shoham established the China Desk of Israeli Law offices GKH, working with clients in Israel and China, and in 2010 organized the DLD Global Beijing Reception at the Ullens Centre for Contemporary Art (UCCA). The same year she became Co-Founder of MedEvents, the first company in Israel for producing conferences for the Bio-Med industry, and just recently, in January 2011, Turbo-Tal co-founded Evolero. 
The company`s basic idea as she describes it, is building up online tools for offline events, that are based on social media. "We are working on the next evolution of events online", Tal Shoham at DLD Tel Aviv argues, "because events are about people. They are social networks, too". In this respect, Evolero is going to develop specific solutions based on the personalities attending an event. "Events should happen simultaneously online and offline", Tal adds. To find out more about Tal Shoham`s innovative thoughts, go the video below.

snippet.title: DLD Tel Aviv 2011 - Interview with Michael Conrad
snippet.description: His mission is a very precise one: to turn "great, creative people into great, creative leaders". Michael Conrad, founder and president of the Berlin School of Creative Leadership at Steinbeis University Berlin, joined the DLD Tel Aviv Summit to explore, whether there might be a chance for a Berlin School-DLD-Partnership. Now he is enthusiastic, because the synergetic potential as he sees it, couldn`t be better. Fostering global discourse on creative leadership in media, entertainment, advertising, journalism, marketing and design, Conrad sees the Berlin School`s role in focusing on a "culture of communication, that leads to cult brands". To learn, why Conrad is deeply fascinated by hackers and their practices, go to the video below.

snippet.title: DLD Tel Aviv 2011 - Interview with Gregory Blatt
snippet.description:
As Head of Marketing and Communications of the Lausanne based company Solar Impulse, Gregory Blatt at DLD Tel Aviv is thrilled to be surrounded by such a big number of entrepreneurs and risk taking founders. When psychiatrist and aeronaut Bertrand Piccard, having made the first non-stop-around-the-world balloon flight, eight years ago launched the project together with Andrew Borschberg, engineer and pilot, not anyone believed in their dream, to fly day and night without fuel, only powered by solar energy.
 
However, after seven years of feasibility studies, simulation, tests and construction, Piccard and Borschberg finally were able to achieve their first solar day-and-night-flight in history, taking them 26 hours, 10 minutes and 19 seconds. So, another vision has come true, as Blatt puts it, proving Jules Verne`s credo: "All that is impossible, remains to be achieved". To learn more about Solar Impulse, go to the video below.

snippet.title: DLD Tel Aviv 2011 - Interview with Hila Oren
snippet.description: She truly understands the DNA of global cities of today. As General Director of the Tel Aviv Global City Administration, Hila Oren at the DLD Tel Aviv summit clearly defines the city`s global role model qualities in being an international centre, able to combine both: business and culture. Creativity Oren states as a core value of this never sleeping city of around 380 000 residents, counting over 4500 start ups. For her, Tel Avivians are "entrepreneurs by character, who are not afraid of failure". And charmingly she compliments DLD as being Tel Aviv`s twin sister: "Both share the same spirit".

snippet.title: DLD Tel Aviv 2011 - Interview with Zell Students
snippet.description:
The Zell Entrepreneurship Program is designed for outstanding students with proven business and leadership abilities in their final year of studies. The program, which is taught in English, provides students with practical tools and theoretical knowledge to establish and operate an entrepreneurial venture, from the inception of an idea to fruition of a company producing value. This year-long academic program begins in the summer and continues through the academic year. In addition to establishing a venture, students will participate in courses and workshops in various areas that are particularly relevant to business entrepreneurs. They also will participate in an entrepreneurship workshop that consists of lectures and meetings with entrepreneurs, investors and professionals involved in various stages of establishing a venture. The program also includes a 10-day study tour abroad. The program's admissions requirements include an outstanding academic record, a familiarity with business entrepreneurship and a passion for excellence.

At DLD Tel Aviv (#dldtelaviv) we got the chance to talk to three Zell students, Or Ben-Oz, Gon Ben David, and Aaron Scott Dubin.

snippet.title: DLD Tel Aviv 2011 - Interview with Assaf Biderman
snippet.description:
Assaf Biderman is moving like a whirlwind through cities. Once gone, the mind-set of urban planners is tossed upside down and not only a few concepts are broken in pieces and make way for a slightly more revolutionary approach. His track record speaks for itself. As advisor, he is working in partnership with the most innovative city administrations and industry members worldwide.  Facing the challenges of increasing urbanisation, Assaf focuses on how distributed technologies (like your smartphone) can be used to improve our understanding of cities and create a more sustainable future living in urban environments.
As Associate Director of the MIT SENSEable City Laboratory, he was involved in enigmatic projects like the Trash Track (mapping the real-time movement of thousands of tagged trash items in Seattle) or the Copenhagen Wheel (hybrid bicycle wheels with environmental sensors for the City of Copenhagen).
At DLD Tel Aviv, we got the chance to talk to him about the "City as the Internet". His exuberant passion for the visionary medication he offers is inarguably overwhelming - and has left many with a brain crush on him. Watch the video below to explore the ideas he shared between the mayor's office and the conference stage.

snippet.title: DLD Tel Aviv 2011 - Interview with Stav Shaffir
snippet.description:
She hasn't slept for more than four hours straight since the 14th of July, and never has been so happy. Still, there is no sign of fatigue when I got the chance to talk to the social activist Stav Shaffir at the DLD Tel Aviv Summit. Stav is one of the protest leaders of the movement for social justice and inclusion in Israel. Describing it as a "wide open social network filled with hope", she believes that optimism is the key to stand together for a change.
Even though the current security issue in Israel adumbrates the movement for social justice, the protesters decrease in numbers and the tents have long disappeared at Rothschild Boulevard, she is burning of hope that the movement will outwear the winter and is here to stay. Despite the cleavages of Israeli society -- class, religion, ethnicity -- this summer has shown that there is a common-ground for an Israeli society as a whole. This society already exists and it's on the government now to fix the broken connection to their sovereign, the people. "A revolution is not a matter of one summer or spring," she concludes, "this is just the beginning."

snippet.title: DLD10 - TV Spot
Video Value (Adam Valkin, Jeremy Allaire, Jason Glickman, Axel Schmiegelow, D.Kirkpatrick) | DLD09
snippet.description: A talk about the future and importance of web-TV. Will it change television? And how influences web-video advertisment.

snippet.title: DLD09 - A Black Mountain College for the 21st Century
snippet.description: Discussion about a new model of art schools. The black mountain college serves as an example. Moreover reports from artists about their contemporary projects.

snippet.title: DLD09 - Women Power
snippet.description: The panelists discuss what is remarkable about womens leadership and their unique qualities. They talk about the role of women in society and in the business world.

snippet.title: DLD09 - Telling Stories
snippet.description: The panelist share their personal approach to storytelling via blogging, film, video mesaging or design. Being the oldest form of communication, the internet revolutionises the way we tell stories today.

snippet.title: DLD09 - Software
snippet.description: The future of software lies in its relationship with the Cloud: the knowledge centre of the future. For software to succeed it has to demonstrate multi-platform usage, with greater speed, precision and usability in accessing and managing content. A group of experts exchange ideas on the future of software business models and design.

snippet.title: Simplicity (G.Wagener, C.Ratti, C.Schläffer, G.Roth, J.Hayzlett, A.Bly) | DLD09
snippet.description: This panel values the essential. It explores the laws of simplicity, and simplicity as a success factor in business and design. Does real beauty lie in simplicity? Panellists discuss the art of understatement and the resonance of leaving space.

snippet.title: Reflection on a Crisis (John Brockman, Nassim Taleb, Daniel Kahneman) | DLD09
snippet.description: Daniel Kahnemann and Nassim Taleb discuss biases, the illusion of patterns as well es the perception of risk and denial.

snippet.title: Predictably Irrational (Dan Ariely, Professor of Behavioral Economics at Duke University) | DLD09
snippet.description: Dan Ariely, Professor of Behavioral Economics at Duke University, explains how people act in the marketplace and how they decide under different emotional states. He exemplifies this based on visual illussions.

snippet.title: DLD09 - Philanthrocapitalism
snippet.description: Matthew Bishop leads a discussion on the new age of charity an social entrepreneurship. The participants illuminate different systems and ideas for investing private wealth back into the society. They talk about the importance of such projects, present their own charity visions and call on the public to help the poor.

snippet.title: On Leadership (Don Tapscott, Brad Anderson, Peter Hirshberg) | DLD09
snippet.description: Social networking is becoming social production. The discussion is about the factors that simulate flexibility and productivity at work.

snippet.title: DLD09 - On Creative Commons
snippet.description: Joi Ito discusses the idea of copyright and Creative Commons in the 21st century.

snippet.title: DLD09 - New Realities
snippet.description: The panelists face the question how the financial and business realities look alike in a world of financial crisis. They talk about structural changes and chances.

snippet.title: New Media Models (Tyler Brulé, Jeff Jarvis, Jochen Wegner, Carolyn McCall, M.Arrington) | DLD09
snippet.description: The panelists are talking about future business models for journalism. Its about new media strategies and the importance of the world wide web. What is the medium of the future and what happens to the traditional print media are raised questions?

snippet.title: DLD09 - Knowledge in the Age of Abundance
snippet.description: The internet is a reflection of our todays society. David Weinberger is talking about the new structure of knowledge.

snippet.title: Internet Politics (Mark Gorenberg, Jack Hidary, Randi Zuckerberg, Micah Sifry, Jeff Jarvis) | DLD09
snippet.description: Barack Obama has been named the first „Internet President. The panelists discuss how technology is changing the way politics work. They mention new social media tools and its impact on political campaigning and fundraising.

snippet.title: DLD09 - Hot Earth & Deep Sea
snippet.description: Environmental warriors and adventurers about their perspectives on nature, sustainability and relief.

snippet.title: DLD09 - Hispanic Markets
snippet.description: The spanish speaking population is one of the fastest growing markets. But its not ONE market, because the cultures fall in love with different things. The panelists discuss the differences between various hispanic cultures and factors that guarantee success.

snippet.title: DLD09 - Global Challenges
snippet.description: Industry leaders discuss the challenges in a world ruled by globalization.They underline the fact that the most important resource are people. Economy has to invest in education. They talk future prospects, ecological problems and the possibilities going along with the current economic crisis.

snippet.title: DLD09 - The Future of Organic Design
snippet.description: Nature should be the main role model for design. The panelists are presenting their visions and talking about design in the 21st century.

snippet.title: DLD09 - Fashion and Business
snippet.description: Marc Ecko and Xavier Court are talking about fashion business and philosophy behind their businesses. They explain their marketing approaches through print magazines, internet and viral campaigns. Moreover they are telling why Airforce One is a different Airforce One, when used by Barack Obama.

snippet.title: DLD09 - Education
snippet.description: Over the past few years the internet has revolutionized the way we seek for information. It has become the main source of information and knowledge. New technologies enable companies to develop education services that will also revolutionize the way we learn. The digital education sector is the next big market opportunity for savvy content and technology providers. The panelists talk about the opportunities of „digital education. They discuss technologies and business models.

snippet.title: DLD09 - Eastern Europe
snippet.description: The Eastern markets are rising fast. The panelists/entrepreneurs talk about their projects, innovations and future directions.

snippet.title: DLD09 - David Kirkpatrick meets Mark Zuckerberg
snippet.description: David Kirkpatrick interviews Mark Zuckerberg on his comany's growth, philosophy and privacy issues. Zuckerberg announces an extensive user growth on the German market.

snippet.title: DLD09 - Creative Collaboration The string quartet case-study
snippet.description: A string quartet case study conducted by Itay Talgam.

snippet.title: DLD09 - Conversation on Communications
snippet.description: Martin Varsavsky and René Obermann talking about the current situation and the future of global communication and digital network markets.

snippet.title: DLD09 - Competitive Compassion
snippet.description: Chris Weeks is talking about humanitarian aid and disaster management based on examples of Deutsche Post.

snippet.title: Cloud Computing (Marissa Mayer, Werner Vogels, Russ Daniels, Spencer Reiss) | DLD09
snippet.description: Cloud computing is about accessibility to data without being tied to a personal comoputer. The more efficient way is to store information in a virtual brain. The panelists discuss oppotunities and frontiers.

snippet.title: DLD09 - City Design
snippet.description: The panelists discuss about the future of architecture using Dubai as an example for visionary projects. They emphasize the limitations of the construction-boom due to financial crisis but also see the cultural mission that city building contains.

snippet.title: DLD09 - China, Designing its Way out of the Crisis
snippet.description: Feng Jun presents several technical design innovations from china such as a MP6 pen which recognizes visual tags at mark and delivers instant information.

snippet.title: About Robots (Dan Dubno, Raffaello D'Andrea, Roth & Tevet, Segej Lupashin, Amir Shapiro) | DLD09
snippet.description: The 21st century has ushered in fascinating new technologies and innovations in the world of robots. This panel look at the role that robots will play in our daily life and future society. Can robots ultimately replace humans? And if we one day find ourselves playing a robot Badminton partner, should we be elated or concerned? Where do the boundaries lie and how can robots impact and enhance our lives? Panellists present some of the most sophisticated robot creations, and discuss robot ethics.

snippet.title: 100 Million Uniques (Mitchell Baker, Jossi Vardi, Chad Hurley, Samir Arora) | DLD09
snippet.description: What makes a product compelling? Why do other vanish? The panelists discuss the emotional aspects and the international social power of the most successful web products.

snippet.title: DLD 2008 - Martha Stewart & Tyler Brûlé about "Style Guide" (2/3)
snippet.description:
From the award-winning magazine, Martha Stewart Living, to the bestselling product lines that bear her name, Martha Stewart has become America's most trusted guide to stylish living. Raised in Nutley, New Jersey, in a family with six children, Martha's passion for cooking, gardening and homekeeping developed in her childhood home.

Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia (MSLO) holds an expansive multimedia portfolio, including award-winning properties such as the magazines Martha Stewart Living and Martha Stewart Weddings, as well as Martha Stewart Living Radio on SIRIUS Satellite Radio. Martha has written dozens of bestselling books on cooking, decorating, gardening and other domestic arts. The company also offers a broad range of branded merchandise for the home, including a line of Martha Stewart Collection home products available exclusively at Macy's.

Martha Stewart has been awarded numerous honors and distinctions from the worlds of business, education, television, media, culinary arts, and retail, with her most recent award including the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2007 Food Network South Beach Wine & Food Festival.

snippet.title: YouTube Reporter am DLD 2008 - Lars Hinrichs
snippet.description:
Lars Hinrichs is co-founder and Managing Director of Xing, formally known as OpenBC. Lars 

started his career as an entrepreneur in 1998 at the age of 22 after working as a consultant at 

different new media firms.

In 1998 Lars initiated "politics digital" a well received and award winning platform in the 

area of politics and new media. In 2000 Lars established Boettcher Hinrichs AG, a consulting 

company and development house for enterprise communication.

Since 2001 Lars has concentrated on being an investment and funding advisor as he has 

accomplished several successful financing rounds for various enterprises. Lars advises 

portfolio companies with business development and business building strategies.

With his broad spectrum of activities and high level memberships in various organizations, e.g. 

the Entrepreneurs Organization (EO), Lars has an excellent network of contacts worldwide. The 

idea of enabling networking between his contacts has inspired him to build up openBC.

snippet.title: YouTube Reporter Interview (David de Rothschild, Founder of Adventure Ecology) | DLD15
snippet.description:
In 2005, David founded Adventure Ecology, an independently run organisation that uses adventure, education and the arts to address global sustainability issues.

His commitment to the environment has sent him to some of the world's most remote and fragile regions. In 2006 David spent over 100 days crossing The Arctic from Russia to Canada, which saw him become one of only 42 people, and the youngest British person to ever reach both geographical poles. Prior to his 2006 'Top of the World Arctic Expedition', David had already become one of only 14 people ever to traverse the continent of Antarctica, and was part of a team that during it's double traverse broke the world record for the fastest ever crossing of the Greenland Icecap.

In early 2007 David completed writing the 'Live Earth Global Warming Survival Handbook', which was the official companion book to the Live Earth concert series.

David is a Judge for the Observer Ethical Awards. A National Geographic 'Emerging Explorer'. A 'Young Global Leader' for the World Economic Forum and in September 2007 GQ Magazine gave him the accolade of 'Environmentalist of the Year'.

'DLD is the one conference where you can truly find and incredible depth of creativity, vision and passion'

snippet.title: YouTube Reporter am DLD 2008 - Reid Hoffman
snippet.description:
Interview mit dem Chairman und President von LinkedIn, Reid Hoffman, während des DLDs in 

München.

 Reid was LinkedIn's founding CEO for the first four years before moving to his role as 

Chairman and President, Products in February 2007. While CEO, Reid built the company to over 9 

million members and profitability; Linkedin now has over 17 million members worldwide.

Prior to LinkedIn, Reid was Executive Vice President of PayPal. At PayPal, Reid was in charge 

of all business relationships: business development, corporate development, international, 

government relations, and banking/payments infrastructure. During his tenure at PayPal, Hoffman 

was instrumental to the acquisition by eBay and was responsible for partnerships with Intuit, 

Visa, MasterCard and Wells Fargo.

Reid also has held management roles in large technology companies, including Fujitsu Software 

Corporation and Apple.

Currently, in addition to LinkedIn, Reid serves on the Board of Directors for SixApart and 

Mozilla Corporation (Firefox).

Reid has also invested in a wide range of Web 2.0 companies, including Facebook, Digg, and 

Wikia.

Reid graduated with distinction from Stanford University with a B.S. in Symbolic Systems and 

from Oxford University with a Master's degree in philosophy.

snippet.title: YouTube Reporter am DLD 2008 - Jimmy Wales
snippet.description:
Gründer von Wikipedia und Wikimedia, ehemaliger Vorsitzender der WikimediaFoundation

 Although best known for founding Wikipedia.org, Jimmy Wales has also set up the Wikimedia 

Foundation in 2003 and co-founded Wikia, Inc., in 2004.

As part of his work at Wikia, Inc., Wales is developing a human-powered search engine, Search 

Wikia, which will be based on the same open, transparent, community-driven principles of Wikia 

and Wikipedia.

Recently, The World Economic Forum recognized Wales as one of the "Young Global Leaders" of 

2007. This prestigious award acknowledges the top 250 young leaders across the world for their 

professional accomplishments, their commitment to society, and their potential to contribute to 

shaping the future of the world. Wales also received the "Time 100 Award" in 2006, named one of 

the world's most influential people in the "Scientists & Thinkers" category. Wales received his 

bachelor's degree in finance from Auburn University and his master's in finance from University 

of Alabama.

snippet.title: YouTube Reporter am DLD 2008 - Antonio Rodriguez
snippet.description:
Founder & CEO of www.tabblo.com - A place to make cool stuff with your photos.

Antonio Rodriguez is director of Research and Development for HP's embedded web-to-print team 

within the company's Imaging and Printing Group and is responsible for helping develop 

solutions that make printing from the web as easy as printing from the desktop.

Formerly, he was the founder and chief executive officer of Tabblo, a privately-held developer 

of web-based printing software which HP acquired in March 2007.

At HP, Rodriguez has been instrumental in developing tools that improve the web-printing 

experience and also in creating web-based printing opportunities where none existed before.

Rodiguez began his career at the Boston Consulting Group, where he provided strategy to 

prominent corporations in the high-tech industry. Since then he has also led development on a 

personal server at Memora Corp. and, before Tabblo, was vice president of Engineering at 

MyPublisher, a New York-based company that makes photo books.

Based in Marlborough, Mass., Rodriguez holds a bachelor's degree from Harvard University and 

master's degree in business administration from Stanford University.

snippet.title: YouTube Reporter am DLD 2008 - Dina Kaplan
snippet.description:
Dina Kaplan is the co-founder and COO of blip.tv.

Dina oversees business operations for the company, including media partnerships, advertising and sponsorship deals, distribution deals, PR, marketing and investor relations. Blip.tv is an online television network featuring and promoting the best shows on the Web.

Before blip.tv Dina was an on-air local television news reporter, where she won an Emmy and numerous Associated Press awards for covering stories. Before reporting Dina worked as an associate producer for MTV News and prior to that as the director of research for the White House Counsel.

Dina is a judge for the Webbies; a member of the Producers Guild of America; on the Board of the Socrates Program at the Aspen Institute; on the National Board of Wesleyan University; on the Advisory Board of the Women's Media Center and of WeLoveBeauty.com; and the founder of the New York City Founders Club.

Dina also believes the start-up community in New York City should rise up and take over the entrepreneurs in Silicon Valley whom she suspects have too much hubris.

snippet.title: YouTube Reporter am DLD 2008 - Marissa Mayer
snippet.description:
As Vice President of Search Products & User Experience, Marissa Mayer leads the product management efforts on Google's search products -- web search, images, news, Google Earth, Google Desktop, Google Labs and more.

She joined Google in 1999 as Google's first female engineer and led the user interface and webserver teams at that time. Her efforts have included designing and developing Google's search interface, internationalizing the site to more than 100 languages, defining Google News, Gmail, and Orkut, and launching more than 100 features and products on Google.com. Several patents have been filed on her work in artificial intelligence and interface design.

Marissa has taught classes at Stanford, who has recognized her with the Centennial Teaching Award and the Forsythe Award.

Prior to joining Google, Marissa worked at the UBS research lab (Ubilab) in Zurich, Switzerland and at SRI International in Menlo Park, CA.

Marissa has been featured in various publications, including Newsweek ("10 Tech Leaders of the Future") and Business 2.0 ("Silicon Valley Dream Team").

Graduating with honors, Marissa received an M.S. in Computer Science from Stanford University.

snippet.title: YouTube Reporter am DLD 2008 - Stephanie Czerny
snippet.description:
Stephanie Czerny has been working for Hubert Burda Media for more than 10 years. She is a curious person and loves to actively connect ideas, people and businesses, most importantly in the fields of media, internet and arts. She loves to discuss; "the next big thing" and "media in transition" is her favourite conversational topic.

She is currently Managing Director at Hubert Burda Media R&D, Marketing & Communications, an assignment she shares with Dr. Marcel Reichart as well as being co-founder and co-host for DLD.

In 2007, she founded two successful crossmedia communities for Hubert Burda Media: burdastyle.com and hallohund.de.

For several years now she has tried to learn the fine art of juggling, especially between family and job, and if you don't find her hacking her Blackberry, she hides as a fervent birdwatcher in Bavarian Alps.

snippet.title: YouTube Reporter am DLD 2008 - Patrick Walker
snippet.description:
Patrick joined Google in January 2006 to lead the development of content strategy and partnerships for Google Video in Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

He has over 15 years of experience in the media industry, including his tenure as General Manager of International Video Services for RealNetworks, where he was instrumental in launching Real's first premium audio and video services in Europe, Asia and Latin America, as well as developing direct-to-consumer broadband video products with partners such as UEFA, BBC Worldwide and Channel 4.

Patrick began his career as a TV producer for Japan's public broadcaster, NHK. While in Tokyo, he produced and directed award-winning educational and documentary TV programmes and participated in the launch of the world's first HDTV channel.

Patrick holds a Master's degree in International Administration, Planning and Social Policy from Harvard and a Bachelor's degree in Journalism from the University of Southern California.

snippet.title: DLD 2008 - Challenges for a global brand (Full Version)
snippet.description:
Olaf Göttgens spricht zum Thema "Challenges for a global brand". Vollversion seines Vortrages am DLD 2008 in München.

 Dr. Olaf Göttgens has been the Vice President in charge of Brand Communications for Mercedes-Benz Cars at Daimler AG since January 2006. In this capacity he is responsible for the brand management as well as for all marketing areas and Mercedes-Benz Classic, including the Mercedes-Benz Museum.

His professional life has included positions at DGM, Anderson Consulting, BBDO Consulting Europe and most recently, as Chief Executive Officer for BBDO Germany.

Dr. Göttgens studied business administration with an emphasis on marketing, trade and information systems and earned his Doctorate on "Success Factors in Stagnant and Shrinking Markets," graduating summa cum laude from the University of Saarland.

Mercedes-Benz, the world´s oldest automaker, is the core brand of the Mercedes-Benz Cars division of Daimler AG. Mercedes-Benz stands for innovative automobiles, quality and safety, sophisticated driving experience and contemporary design and benefits from its unique tradition.

snippet.title: DLD 2008 Highlights - Martha Stewart "Style Guides"
snippet.description:
Highlights des Vortrages "Style Guides" von Martha Stewart. Interviewer: Tyler Brûlé

From the award-winning magazine, Martha Stewart Living, to the bestselling product lines that bear her name, Martha Stewart has become America's most trusted guide to stylish living. Raised in Nutley, New Jersey, in a family with six children, Martha's passion for cooking, gardening and homekeeping developed in her childhood home.

Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia (MSLO) holds an expansive multimedia portfolio, including award-winning properties such as the magazines Martha Stewart Living and Martha Stewart Weddings, as well as Martha Stewart Living Radio on SIRIUS Satellite Radio. Martha has written dozens of bestselling books on cooking, decorating, gardening and other domestic arts. The company also offers a broad range of branded merchandise for the home, including a line of Martha Stewart Collection home products available exclusively at Macy's.

Martha Stewart has been awarded numerous honors and distinctions from the worlds of business, education, television, media, culinary arts, and retail, with her most recent award including the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2007 Food Network South Beach Wine & Food Festival.

snippet.title: YouTube Reporter am DLD 2008 - Paulo Coelho
snippet.description:
Originally from Brazil, Paulo began his career by first joining forces with rock star Raul Seixas, composing 120 songs that revolutionized Brazilian rock music.

In 1986, Paulo walked the Road to Santiago, and reconverted to Christianity, finding, again, the faith bequeathed to him by the Jesuit fathers of his school years. He would later describe this experience in his first book, The Pilgrimage, published in 1987. The following year, his second book, The Alchemist established his worldwide reputation. The novel has already achieved the status of a universally admired modern classic.

Paulo Coelho is an advocate of multiculturalism through his work with UNESCO as a Special Counsellor for Intercultural Dialogues and Spiritual Convergences. Paulo was appointed as United Nations Messenger of Peace in 2007, allowing him to continue to promote intercultural dialogue and to focus on children's needs.

snippet.title: Interview with Daniel Dubno | DLD08
snippet.description:
Daniel Dubno is a pioneer in the use of powerful graphic technologies, satellite imagery, and visualization tools for news coverage. Until recently he was producer and technologist for CBS News in New York, where he coordinated Special Events Unit coverage of major national and international news stories.

Winner of numerous National Emmy awards, Dubno was previously a producer of the 'Eye on America' enterprise reports for the CBS Evening News, and he produced investigative and feature segments for Eye to Eye with Connie Chung, America Tonight and economics coverage for CBS This Morning.

Dan Dubno's technology website, Gizmorama, is one of the most popular technology review sites on the Internet. He also writes a monthly technology column for Discover Magazine and contributes to other science magazines on occasion.

snippet.description:
David Silverman is an animator best known for directing numerous episodes of the animated TV series The Simpsons.

David is largely credited with creating most of the "rules" for drawing The Simpsons. Having started with The Simpsons (in 1987) as one of two animators on "The Tracey Ullman Show," David has recently finished directed "The Simpsons Movie," released this summer 2007.
David has also worked as co-director on Pixar's "Monsters. Inc.," and as story editor on "Ice Age."

For reasons that confound his parents, he plays the tuba. This strange desire has been further acted on by his developement of The Flaming Tuba, pictures above. He performs this mostly at Burning Man, and at venues with no ceilings.

snippet.title: DLD 2008 - Trailer
snippet.description:
DLD

DLD (Digital, Life, Design) is Europe's conference for the 21st century, covering digital innovation, science and culture and bringing together thought leaders from Europe, the Middle-East, America and Asia. The three-day event is chaired by publisher Hubert Burda and investor Joseph Vardi and hosted by Stephanie Czerny and Marcel Reichart.

DLD08 is scheduled for January 20-22, 2008 at HVB Forum in Munich, Germany.
